title: Trump envoys say Ukraine talks were "very meaningful" after Moscow visit
summary: After meeting Putin, President Trump's envoys are expected to discuss a proposal to end the war in Ukraine.
story: President Trump's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, said they held "meaningful discussions" and are encouraged by the talks in Kyiv, part of a trip that began in Moscow, as the latest push to end more than 4½ years of Russia's full-scale invasion continues.
Sunday marked the first time the U.S. envoys had traveled to Ukraine since Mr. Trump returned to office with a pledge to solve the conflict.

Kushner, who is Mr. Trump's son-in-law, told reporters on Sunday that the president has been following the developments of the meetings "very closely" and is working hard to "find a pathway to end this war."
"But not just to end the conflict. What President Trump's been very focused on is how do we create a framework that could actually build, lead to a durable peace," he added.

After two rounds of discussion with the U.S. officials, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the goal was a "just, fair peace" that would ensure there was "never an opportunity to resume aggression against Ukraine."
"We've had very meaningful discussion, substantive, important, and we're very encouraged," Witkoff said, though he acknowledged that Russia and Ukraine will need to make "compromises" to end the war.

"It's going to take both sides to make some compromises and narrow the issues between them and we think we have the ingredients to get to that place," he added. "It is very difficult, but we are committed, we care, and we hope all of that leads to a successful, peaceful diplomatic resolution."

A senior Ukrainian official, who spoke on condition of anonymity as he was not authorized to speak publicly, told The Associated Press that much of the discussion was focused on "how to get through the winter and what can be done before then."
Zelenskyy said that while there was a "positive assessment" of talks, the war with Russia "at the moment" looked likely to continue this winter.

"We very much hope that we will be able to reach agreements with our American partners, and we are counting on the support of our European partners – if the war continues in winter, and this is how it appears at the moment – but even so, the teams today have a positive assessment of our future prospects," Zelenskyy said.
No breakthroughs in Moscow

Witkoff and Kushner held a three-hour meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday in Moscow, where they "discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks," according to a White House official.

Prior to Witkoff and Kushner's departure, Mr. Trump told reporters the envoys were traveling to Ukraine and Russia with a proposal to end the conflict. Mr. Trump said they had had "an idea for peace," and that "there may be a good chance that we'll do it."

After the meeting, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said in a statement that "our American colleagues made serious preparations for this trip," and they had "also formulated a number of ideas regarding possible paths to a settlement," but did not elaborate on what those might be.

At the start of the meeting in Moscow, which was captured on video, Putin asked Kushner and Witkoff to pass on his warm wishes and gratitude to Mr. Trump, and described the situation in Ukraine as "not simple."
Ushakov added that the talks also discussed in "some detail" potential deals between the U.S. and Russia that would be "mutually beneficial."
Both Ukraine and Russia agreed Saturday to pause strikes while the envoys were in the country to allow for talks to take place.

"Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days," presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russia's Tass news agency, saying the decision was tied to Witkoff and Kushner's planned visit to the Ukrainian capital. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy mirrored the decision by halting strikes until Monday.
In his Sunday prayer, Pope Leo XIV renewed his appeal for peace in Ukraine and said he hopes the negotiations will bring results.
"I hope that the efforts undertaken in recent days to resume negotiations will bear concrete fruit and make way for diplomacy," he told the gathered faithful in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican.

The White House official also told CBS News that the U.S. delegation thanked Putin for the release of U.S. Marine veteran Robert Gilman, a 32-year-old teacher who had been imprisoned in Russia since 2022. Gilman was freed and allowed to return home last month. Before his release, Gilman was hospitalized in serious condition after he had allegedly been subjected to severe mistreatment, according to Global Reach, an organization that worked to free him.

title: UN endorses new map that shows Africa's size more accurately
summary: Africa has long been represented as smaller than its real size in maps, which are largely based on an ancient projection.
story: The United Nations General Assembly on Friday endorsed a new world map that represents Africa more accurately in its larger size, a culmination of a recent campaign led by African countries and advocacy groups.

Friday's resolution, which was sponsored by Togo and backed by members of the African Union, was passed with 164 member states voting in favor. Only the U.S. voted against it while six other countries - Serbia, Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova and Ukraine - abstained.

The vote encourages governments and institutions around the world to replace the traditional Mercator map, commonly used since the 16th Century, with the Equal Earth projection that advocates and geographers say shows locations more accurately.

The Mercator projection shows Greenland and Africa as appearing to be about the same size whereas in the Equal Earth projection that shows continents in their true proportions, Africa is 14 times larger than Greenland.
Friday's resolution does not ban the Mercator projection or impose a replacement, but only encourages the use of the Equal Earth projection, the U.N. said in its report.

"Maps shape our understanding of the world," the global body quoted Togo's Foreign Minister Robert Dussey as saying before the vote. "They guide education, nourish the imagination, and influence collective perceptions."

Africa No Filter, one of the lead campaigners for the adoption of the new map, hailed the resolution, adding: "We want to see accurate maps in schools, textbooks, newsrooms, businesses and on the digital platforms billions of people use every day."

Several countries hailed the adoption and urged the adoption of the Equal Earth map. "Changing the map obviously doesn't change the world. But correcting a representation that distorts it is already an act of truth," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on X after the vote.

The Mercator map was designed by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European navigators at sea, but advocates say it distorted landmasses by enlarging regions near the poles such as North America and Greenland while shrinking Africa and South America.
The 2018 Equal Earth projection, on the other hand, follows the Earth's curvature and shows continents in their true proportions.
Geographers say the traditional map is only useful for navigation.
"Outside of that very narrow navigation application, there is no point in using it," according to Mark Monmonier, a Syracuse University professor of geography.

title: Prince Harry finds way to live ‘half-in, half-out’ life Queen Elizabeth refused to endorse: experts
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan's U.K. return with their children echoes the "half-in, half-out" proposal Queen Elizabeth II rejected at Sandringham.
story: Hugo Vickers, author of "Queen Elizabeth II: A Personal History," details how the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's exit and Oprah interview added strain during the late monarch's final years.
Prince Harry may have finally found a way to live the life that his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, refused to endorse.

On Sept. 8, 2022, Britain's longest-reigning monarch died after 70 years on the throne. She was 96. On Aug. 26 this year, Harry and his wife, Meghan Markle, returned to the U.K., where their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, will attend school.

As the Sussexes settle into their new life in Britain, with details about their private home and their children's school closely guarded, royal experts told Fox News Digital that the arrangement recalls the "half-in, half-out" proposal the late queen rejected.
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY

From left: Queen Elizabeth II, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex watch a flypast to mark the centenary of the Royal Air Force from the balcony of Buckingham Palace on July 10, 2018, in London, England. The couple stepped back as senior royals in 2020. They returned to the United Kingdom before Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet started school in September 2026. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Harry may feel vindicated because, superficially, he has created something resembling the freedom he originally wanted," Kinsey Schofield, host of the YouTube show "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. "But I think calling it a victory misunderstands what the queen rejected."

"I see absolutely no reason to believe she would have changed her mind," Schofield said. "Queen Elizabeth spent 70 years protecting the distinction between the crown and the individual. It seems unlikely that one of the defining judgements of her final years would suddenly have become negotiable."

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duke and Duchess of Sussex, leave a service of thanksgiving for the reign of Queen Elizabeth II at St. Paul's Cathedral in London on June 3, 2022, during Platinum Jubilee celebrations marking the monarch's 70 years of service. (Matt Dunham - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

While the Sussexes have returned to the U.K. for an extended stay, they won't resume their roles as working royals. They will live in a private, non-royal residence outside London while maintaining their California home and a property in Portugal. People magazine reported that Meghan is in early talks for a role in the Netflix drama "The Gentlemen."
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE CAUSED QUEEN STRESS IN FINAL YEARS: AUTHOR

On Monday, the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the royal household, sent a letter to senior officials in the government and military, as well as lord lieutenants, the king's personal representatives around the country.
The letter drew a firm line around the Sussexes’ homecoming, reaffirming that the couple will not resume official duties.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family," a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III read, Fox News can confirm. "This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected."

"It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex," the letter added. "Their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and are not used. The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity. In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."
A letter sent on behalf of King Charles on Monday reaffirmed that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not resume official duties. (Isabel Infantes//POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as senior royals in 2020 after describing intense scrutiny from the British press and saying they lacked support from the palace.

"Following conversations with the duke, the queen has written confirming that in stepping away from the work of the royal family it is not possible to continue with the responsibilities and duties that come with a life of public service," a statement from Buckingham Palace read at the time.

From left: Queen Elizabeth II, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex watch a flypast to mark the centenary of the Royal Air Force from the balcony of Buckingham Palace on July 10, 2018, in London, England. The couple stepped back as senior royals in 2020. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
In response, the couple issued a statement of their own, saying: "We can all live a life of service. Service is universal."
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex depart Canada House in London, on Jan. 7, 2020. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital the queen drew a firm line before the couple's departure, insisting the Sussexes could not be "half in, half out" as working royals.

"Her position was simply stated as ‘all in or all out,’" Fordwich said. "While King Charles has maintained that position, he is likely to be more open to private reconciliation and family gatherings, especially if Harry refrains from further public attacks on the family. Prince William, however, remains resistant to any formal restoration of royal duties for Harry."

Prince William, Prince of Wales and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex attend the Committal Service for Queen Elizabeth II at St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle on Sept. 19, 2022, in Windsor, England. (Getty Images)
In 2020, Harry attended the Sandringham Summit at Queen Elizabeth II's Norfolk estate, where senior royals determined the terms of his and Meghan's departure from royal life.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex sits in a car as she attends Queen Elizabeth's state funeral and burial in London on Sept. 19, 2022. (POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

According to People magazine, it was there that the late queen made her position clear. After lengthy discussions, Harry was told there would be no "half-in, half-out" role for the Sussexes. They could not remain working royals while also pursuing independent, income-generating ventures.

In his memoir "Spare," Harry recalled the Sandringham meeting and wrote that he believed the royals would consider five options for the Sussexes. "Option Five" called for a full departure. After about an hour, the queen's private secretary — nicknamed "The Bee" by Harry — distributed drafts of a statement announcing "Option Five." Harry wrote that he was stunned.

From left: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Queen Elizabeth II attend the Queen's Young Leaders Awards Ceremony at Buckingham Palace in London on June 26, 2018. (John Stillwell/WPA Pool/Getty Images)
"Wait. I'm confused," he wrote. "You've already drafted a statement? Before any discussion? Announcing Option Five? In other words, the fix was in this whole time? This summit was just for show?"
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, arrives at Westminster Abbey ahead of the State Funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in London on Sept. 19, 2022. (Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital he believes the palace made a mistake by rejecting the proposal outright.

"In my view, the queen was very badly advised by her representatives over the ‘half in, half out’ policy," he said. "I cannot see any reason in this day and age why it could not work. It shows a level of hypocrisy. Harry and Meghan could have remained in the royal fold without costs to the public purse. And yet, this was deemed unacceptable."
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, and Queen Elizabeth II attend Day 1 of Royal Ascot at Ascot Racecourse in Ascot, England, on June 19, 2018. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Schofield argued the queen had good reason to reject the proposal.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Sandringham House, the royal family's estate in Norfolk, England. (Radcliffe/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images/Getty Images)
"The queen had already learned the dangers of ‘half in, half out’ long before Harry and Meghan proposed it," she explained.

"Prince Edward and Duchess Sophie attempted to maintain commercial careers alongside royal duties, with Edward running his television company and Sophie working in public relations. The arrangement became increasingly uncomfortable for the institution, especially as their professional lives generated headlines that risked trading on their royal connections. Ultimately, they abandoned those careers and became full-time working royals."

Duchess Sophie and Prince Edward depart Soufriere by boat on Day 6 of their Platinum Jubilee royal tour of the Caribbean on April 27, 2022, in Soufriere, Saint Lucia. (Stuart C. Wilson - Pool/Getty Images)

"That experience demonstrated exactly why the lines need to be clear," Schofield continued. "You are either representing the Crown and accepting the restrictions that come with that privilege, or you are pursuing a private, commercial life. Trying to do both inevitably raises questions about royal status, access and whether relationships are being leveraged for personal gain."
Prince Harry told the BBC in 2025 that he's ready for reconciliation. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

Schofield argued senior royals dedicate themselves fully to serving the crown and supporting the monarch as a united front. She said it would have been "unfair" to relax those restrictions for the Sussexes while allowing them to benefit from their royal status. In the queen's eyes, commercial freedom was "incompatible" with royal service.

"The queen might have wanted more family connection with Harry and Meghan, but she wouldn’t have compromised the constitutional aspects of such an arrangement," Fordwich said. "She would also have been deeply wary of the commercial conflicts it could create. It would have set a precedent for other royals wanting to have it both ways."
Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Harry attend the annual Chelsea Flower Show at Royal Hospital Chelsea on May 18, 2015, in London, England. (Julian Simmonds - WPA Pool / Getty Images)
Before Harry and Meghan returned to Britain, Simon Vigar, author of "The Four Wives of Windsor," told Fox News Digital that a "hybrid" model was inevitable.

King Charles III ascended to the throne upon the death of his mother, Queen Elizabeth II, on Sept. 8, 2022. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"[The Sussexes] thought they could have a hybrid role of having a business life and a private life, while also spending a few months in the U.K. supporting the queen," he shared. "Harry believed that was an option, which was whipped away from him."
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY BELIEVED ROYAL FAMILY COULD HAVE ALLOWED A ‘HYBRID’ ROLE: AUTHOR

After stepping back from royal duties, the Sussexes signed lucrative deals with Netflix and Spotify and publicly aired their grievances in interviews, documentaries and Harry's memoir, further straining his relationship with the royal family.
Queen Elizabeth sits with Prince William and Prince Harry in the royal box at Guards Polo Club, Smiths Lawn, Windsor. (Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)
In 2025, Harry told the BBC he was ready for reconciliation and eager to spend more time with his father, who is being treated for an undisclosed form of cancer.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, relocated to California in 2020. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
According to a source close to the Sussexes, Meghan will continue leading her As Ever company from the U.K., while Harry will spend more time working with his U.K.-based charities.
In July, the Sussexes privately met with the king at his Highgrove estate. It was the first time Archie and Lilibet had seen their grandfather since the late queen’s Platinum Jubilee in 2022.
Highgrove House, the king's private residence, in Doughton, Gloucestershire. (Neil Bennett/Mirrorpix/Getty Images)
Schofield questioned whether Harry has any regrets about his grandmother's final years.

(Emilio Morenatti - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
"Harry says he loved his grandmother, and has spoken very warmly about their relationship," she said.

"But some of his choices during her final years became part of an already difficult period for the royal family. Whatever grievances Harry had with the institution, his grandmother was elderly, recently widowed and approaching the end of an entire life of service. There are conversations he can never have with her and decisions he can never revisit with her."

title: Julia Louis-Dreyfus reveals ‘tons’ of friction behind the scenes of ‘Seinfeld’
summary: Julia Louis-Dreyfus opened up on the "Friends Keep Secrets" podcast about the arguments and hard work that shaped "Seinfeld" into a phenomenon.
story: FOX Business contributor Katrina Campins, comedian Rich Vos and comedian Charles McBee joined 'Fox News Saturday Night' to discuss how comedy has evolved alongside society's affinity for political correctness.
Julia Louis-Dreyfus didn't mince words about what it took to make "Seinfeld" a television phenomenon.
The actress, who starred as Elaine Benes, revealed there was "tons" of friction behind the scenes as the cast and creators worked to get the groundbreaking comedy just right.

title: Christine Taylor was asked to lose 10 pounds after landing Marcia Brady role in 'Brady Bunch Movie'
summary: Christine Taylor revealed she was asked to lose 10 pounds for her role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie" during the "Office Ladies" podcast.
story: "The Brady Bunch" stars Barry Williams and Christopher Knight share how they’ve stayed connected over 55 years since the show’s debut.
Christine Taylor landed her dream role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie" – but the part came with a catch.

The "Brady Bunch Movie" star recalled the uncomfortable demand she received after landing the role of Marcia Brady during the "Office Ladies" podcast, revealing she was "embarrassed" but agreed to do it because "that was just how things went" in Hollywood at the time.
Taylor landed the role of Marcia after starring in a live show called "The Real Live Brady Bunch."
The actress had been obsessed with Marcia Brady for years and had seen "every single episode ... backwards and forwards, inside out."
MICHELLE PFEIFFER SAYS SHE FELT 'HUMILIATED' FOLLOWING HER AUDITION FOR HER BREAKTHROUGH ROLE IN 'GREASE 2'

"And then out-of-the-blue one day, I mean, out of the blue on my answering machine in 1990, whatever year this was, 92 or 93, I got a message from Sherwood Schwartz calling me, just cold calling me saying, 'I would love to meet with you...'" she recalled.
For Taylor, getting a personal call from "The Brady Bunch" creator was the kind of Hollywood moment she never expected – and one she wished she had preserved.
"It was a pinch me moment that I cannot believe to this day that I still didn't keep my little tape from the answering machine," she added.
But beneath the disbelief, Taylor said she had no doubts about whether she was right for the role.

That confidence appeared to carry her through the casting process, which Taylor remembered as surprisingly straightforward.
"I'm fairly sure that I met with them and that was pretty much it," she recalled. "They didn't tell me I got it, but I never had to go back in and audition solo again."
Instead, Taylor read with different actors who would later portray her siblings – Jan and Cindy.

title: King Charles III clarifies Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not resume royal duties after UK move

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family," a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III read, Fox News can confirm. "This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected."

title: Michael Rapaport slams 'clown' Macklemore for anti-Israel performance
summary: Michael Rapaport called Macklemore a "clown" after the rapper chanted "Free Palestine" and performed "Hind's Hall" at Ed Sheeran's MetLife shows.
story: Fox News correspondent CB Cotton reports on rapper Macklemore facing backlash over anti-Israel comments while performing at an Ed Sheeran concert on ‘Fox Report.’
Michael Rapaport slammed Macklemore as a "clown" after the rapper brought his pro-Palestinian message to Ed Sheeran’s concert stage.

Macklemore, 43, repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind's Hall" while opening for Sheeran, 35, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, during shows on Friday and Saturday nights.

On Saturday, Rapaport, 56, who is Jewish and has become one of Hollywood’s most outspoken pro-Israel voices since Hamas' Oct. 7 attack, ripped Macklemore, born Benjamin Haggerty, in a blistering post on X.
BLACK CROWES FACE BACKLASH AFTER CHRIS ROBINSON SHUTS DOWN U.S.A. CHANT AND CALLS FANS 'IGNORANT'

"Imagine going to see Ed Sheeran & this absolute no talent none singer non rapping non dancing clown Macklemore is opening & because he actually has no act or specific skill set he’s jumping around like dkc carrying on about a genocide that never happened in Gaza," Rapaport wrote, adding "This is a nightmare."
Michael Rapaport ripped Macklemore after the rapper chanted "Free Palestine" and performed an anti-Israel song while opening for Ed Sheeran. (Bobby Bank/Getty Images; Kieran Frost/Redferns)
In another critical post on X, the comedian questioned Sheeran’s decision to bring Macklemore on as an opening act.
ED SHEERAN CONCERT WORKERS HOSPITALIZED AFTER FORKLIFT INCIDENT IN DETROIT: REPORT
"So Ed Sheeran is ok with this p--- stain opening up for him? Sweet Ed Sheeran?" Rapaport wrote.
Rapaport also reposted an article about the backlash to Macklemore's political messaging following the concerts, writing, "Calling this dude a ‘Rapper' is disrespectful to any actual ‘Rapper.’"
ISRAEL, JEWS TARGETED WORLDWIDE AS WELL-FUNDED LEFTIST, ISLAMIST GROUPS JOIN FOR ‘NAKBA 78’ PROTESTS
Fox News Digital has reached out to Macklemore and Sheeran's representatives for comment.

In a video that Rapaport posted from the Friday night show, Macklemore, who wore a keffiyeh tied around his neck, was seen repeatedly chanting "Say free, free Palestine!" while music played as he walked around the stage and held up his microphone.

Macklemore, who will be opening for Sheeran during the U.S. leg of the "Shape of You" singer's "Loop Tour," also delivered a speech in which he said that he wanted to use stages across America to advocate for Palestine.
Macklemore opened for Ed Sheeran at the singer's concerts at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Friday and Saturday nights. (Morgan Hancock/Getty Images)
ISRAELI PM NETANYAHU ARGUES PUBLIC OPINION SHIFT ON ISRAEL 'CORRELATES ALMOST 100%' TO SOCIAL MEDIA

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine," Macklemore said in a video shared on social media.
"I said, ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them," he continued.

"I have an 11-year-old daughter, her name is Sloan, she’s here tonight. And if any of you guys are parents, then you know that that love that you have for your kids cannot be put into words, right? I want to see her grow up, I want to see her go to school, to fall in love, to figure out meaning, purpose, joy, her existence on this planet. I want it to be the most beautiful possible."

"And I think that every single human being that walks this earth deserves that exact same feeling. To know safety and peace before they know the sound of violence, to know the sound of laughter on a playground before planes and bombs, for parents to be able to say bye to their kids in the morning and not have to wonder if this is going to be the last time they kiss their child goodbye."

"And if I let that fear I felt on the plane yesterday stop me from speaking my heart in order to keep my own comfort and the audience’s comfort, that is the day I no longer continue to be on stage," Macklemore added. "So, I say, ‘Free Palestine!’"
Rapaport is Jewish and has become one of Israel's most outspoken defenders in Hollywood. (Charles Sykes/Bravo via Getty Images)
RAGE AGAINST THE MACHINE'S TOM MORELLO FACES BACKLASH AFTER SINGING AT NYC ICE PROTEST RALLY
Macklemore concluded his speech by calling for the freedom of other countries, including America, and blasting U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
"I say, free America, free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran, and all the people in America who have to live in fear because of this terrorist organization, ICE," he said.
HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS

Following his speech, Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," a song inspired by the 2024 pro-Palestinian campus demonstrations," as footage from Gaza, pro-Palestinian protests, images of Israeli soldiers and pro-Palestinian messages were displayed on the stadium’s large screens.

The title of the song refers to Hamilton Hall, the Columbia University building that pro-Palestinian students occupied in April 2024 and renamed in honor of a 6-year-old Palestinian girl killed in the Israel-Gaza war. The lyrics in "Hind's Hall" praised the anti-Israel encampments and protests on college campuses across the country and called out President Biden, the police and the music industry.
RAPPER FACES $2.8M LAWSUIT AFTER AXING OPENING ACT FROM TOUR FOLLOWING HER POLITICAL RANT
Macklemore also repeated his pro-Palestinian messaging during Sheeran’s second MetLife Stadium show Saturday night, again calling for "Free Palestine" and performing his protest song "Hind’s Hall."
Macklemore said one of the reasons that he joined Sheeran's tour was to share his pro-Palestinian message. (Kieran Frost/Redferns)
While some audience members cheered Macklemore's comments and joined the "Free Palestine" chant, the rapper's performance was met with backlash from other attendees.

One concertgoer said on X that he brought his wife and two daughters to Friday’s show as longtime Sheeran fans, but left disappointed after Macklemore’s set turned political. The fan said his daughters looked "completely confused" when Macklemore began chanting "Free Palestine," adding that he had taken them to "an Ed Sheeran concert, not to have an opening act lecture them about Middle East politics."

He said his family left their seats during Macklemore’s performance and returned after the rapper finished, praising Sheeran’s show as "phenomenal" but criticizing the singer for allowing Macklemore to perform again Saturday. "Friday might have been Macklemore’s decision. Saturday was yours," the concertgoer wrote, adding, "Tonight, you lost four of them. And I suspect plenty more."

Another concertgoer said he attended Saturday’s show in a company suite with 35 other people and was "embarrassed" and "shocked" by Macklemore’s set. The attendee said he had "always been a Macklemore fan," but after the rapper’s "political stunt," he could no longer support him or his music.
"When you go WOKE, you have to be prepared to lose fans," he wrote.
The concertgoer also denounced Sheeran for allowing Macklemore to return to the stage Saturday after the backlash from the previous night.
"After it happened on Friday, it should have immediately been stopped," he wrote, adding that he went to the show to hear "amazing music," not "Free Palestine" rants.
Sheeran was also criticized on social media for allowing Macklemore to open for him again at Saturday's concert. (Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images)
Two other concertgoers told Ynet, the English edition of Israel's largest new website, that they were unfamiliar with Macklemore before the show and unaware that he would be performing.
"We only found out there and we were in shock. It was really horrifying," they said.

"We immediately thought about everything our people have been through and how, even when we’re abroad, we still have to feel this antisemitism," they continued. "It was even harder because friends of ours were killed in the war and murdered at Nova. It was like a knife in the heart to hear him sing that way and hear people cheering."
The concertgoers said that some of the members in their group began crying and left the show before Sheeran's performance.
However, some social media users praised Macklemore for speaking up and expressed their support for the rapper's message.

"Huge respect for Ed Sheeran, but seeing Macklemore use his voice for Palestine made this moment mean so much more," one fan wrote on Instagram. "Respect to every artist who refuses to stay silent and uses their platform to speak up for humanity. Macklemore, we hear you."
"LOVE Macklemore, and good on him using his platform to speak out….his messaging is always spot on. Peace," another agreed.
"Free free Palestine. Love to Macklemore. Stay true," one fan chimed in.
The rapper also slammed ICE during his speech. (ARNAUD FINISTRE / AFP via Getty Images)
"this was from last night!! I hope you get to perform this again tonight too!" a fan wrote alongside a clip from Macklemore's set.
"So happy we get to witness such history!" one fan commented.
"Honestly I loved this part of the concert !" another wrote.

"Music has always been a vital platform for human rights advocacy, not just mindless escape," wrote one X user. "Calling for peace, safety, and equality for Palestinians, Congolese, and Sudanese isn't antisemitic—it's pro-humanity. Macklemore explicitly stands for collective liberation and love."

"Art has always been political, why are you annoyed at an artist giving context to a song he released about the current state of the world you live in?" another fan commented on X. "Also, he was an opener, they could’ve just skipped his set! Although I hope Macklemore sings it louder next time!"

Meanwhile, the Israeli-American Council launched a petition calling for Macklemore to be removed from Sheeran’s remaining tour dates.

"This was an Ed Sheeran concert – not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event," the petition read. "The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda."
Macklemore previously called the war in Gaza a "genocide." (Kristy Sparow/Getty Images)

Macklemore has been outspoken in his support for Palestinians since the start of the Israel-Hamas war. In November 2023, Macklemore spoke at a pro-Palestinian rally in Washington, D.C., where he said, "I don’t know enough. But I know enough that this is a genocide."

The rapper's political messaging has also sparked backlash before. In 2024, he addressed criticism after saying "f--- America" during a pro-Palestinian charity concert in Seattle, later writing that he remained "unwavering in my support for a Free Palestine."

South Africa brought a genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice, which ordered Israel in 2024 to take steps to prevent acts of genocide while the case proceeds. Israel has strongly denied accusations of genocide, saying its military campaign is directed at Hamas, not Palestinian civilians, and that it warns civilians to evacuate ahead of attacks while taking steps to comply with international law.

title: William Fichtner has ‘never’ regretted turning down roles and refuses to cross ‘certain lines’ in Hollywood
summary: William Fichtner told Fox News Digital that he's never regretted turning down a role if it crosses his boundaries, even if they end up being successful.
story: Fichtner told Fox News Digital he feels very comfortable turning down film roles when they cross his boundaries.
"Lucky" star William Fichtner has no problem turning down a role if it crosses his boundaries.
During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 69-year-old actor shared that he has "never" regretted saying no to a project, even if it turned out to be a big success.

"I've been a bit pickier and choosier at moments in my life where I probably didn't have a right to be," he said. "But if I didn't believe it, if I didn't think that I could do something with it, and there are certain lines that I just don't cross. But, if I don't have a belief in it, then I have a little bit of a fear that I don't want to be bad, and I just won't take the journey."

He explained that he doesn't "hold it as a badge of honor," that he has said no to a few "jobs that were really good money," and described knowing immediately that "this isn't happening" when reading something he doesn't like.
Fichtner shared that he's never regretted turning down a role, even if it ended up being successful. (Brianna Bryson/FilmMagic)

Fichtner plays Wayne Whittaker in the Apple TV miniseries "Lucky,' which aired its series finale, titled "All Good Things," on Wednesday, Aug. 19.

story: Family therapist Robin Hamilton told Fox News Digital that Braun must be "deliberate" about quality time with his kids.

"You want to keep their personal lives personal and their parents' celebrity lives theirs," Hamilton told Fox News Digital. Just keep it separate because people are going to be approaching these kids. They're going to ask them questions... So they have to be prepared.

"Prepare the kids to navigate those questions and how people are going to approach them if they want them to be in the public life. I would say like being deliberate about spending quality time where there's nobody commenting on you, there are no cameras there and just, you know, not putting all that pressure on the kids right now, because it's a lot."

title: Bunnie Xo reveals shocking physical toll of divorce from Jelly Roll
summary: Bunnie Xo revealed she lost 20 pounds and needed IVs during her Jelly Roll divorce, detailing the devastating physical toll of her heartbreak.
story: Jelly Roll tells Fox News Digital what it means to him to celebrate the 60th Academy of Country Music Awards.
Bunnie Xo revealed the physical toll heartbreak has taken on her as she navigates her divorce from Jelly Roll.

Bunnie Xo detailed previous strains in her relationship with Jelly Roll after news broke about their divorce. (Christopher Polk)

As Bunnie picks up the pieces after the end of her nearly decade-long marriage, she said she’s entered a new chapter focused on putting herself first without feeling guilty about it.

title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
summary: Christie Brinkley reveals how she keeps all three adult children coming home and why losing both parents deepened her devotion to family time.
story: Christie Brinkley, star of ‘American Summer,’ explains why losing both parents made family time more precious and shares how she keeps her children close.
Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest.
The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections.
The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital those themes aren't just on-screen. They're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to.

The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas.
CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS
Christie Brinkley's new movie, "American Summer, hit theaters Sept. 4. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids. ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that.

Christie Brinkley and daughters Sailor Lee Brinkley-Cook and Alexa Ray Joel arrive at the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit 2017 launch event at Center415 Event Space in New York City Feb. 16, 2017. (GC Images)
"It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared.
"And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing."
Christie Brinkley's children — Alexa Ray Joel, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook and Sailor Brinkley-Cook — remain a central part of her life. (Getty Images)

The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents.
WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE

After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9.

"I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad."
Alexa Ray Joel and Christie Brinkley appear onstage at the Big Apple Circus in New York City Feb. 1, 2020. (Getty Images for Big Apple Circus)
Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them."
Christie Brinkley's parents attend a pageant in Hawaii, date unknown. (Corbis via Getty Images)

Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home.

"I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world."
Family came first for Steve Guttenberg, who paused his acting career to help care for his father, Stanley Guttenberg. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"American Summer" is described as a homage to families in small-town America. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

Family continues to be an essential part of Brinkley's life. She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her.
For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family.
Christie Brinkley and Sailor Brinkley Cook attend the Solving Kids Cancer Annual Hamptons Luncheon at Tutto II Giorno in Southampton, N.Y., on Aug. 4, 2025. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "This [story] takes us back before there were cellphones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cellphones more often and just connecting with loved ones.

"And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach. I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'
Steve Guttenberg and Christie Brinkley in a scene from "American Summer." (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections. ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again."
"It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said.

Christie Brinkley poses with son Jack at the opening night arrivals for Michael Moore's "The Terms of My Surrender" on Broadway at the Belasco Theatre in New York City Aug. 10, 2017. (Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic)
Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher, a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Christie Brinkley attends Best Friends Animal Society's The Spirit of the Sanctuary"benefit Aug. 24, 2026, at Jill Rappaport's Last Buck Ranch in Water Mill, N.Y. (Getty Images)

"I've always been a birdwatcher," she said. "On my Instagram, I have a bird feeder, and if you go back, you'll see lots and lots of pictures of the birds at my bird feeder. And I was just reading that birdwatching is back in full force for young people, too. People want to connect with nature. They want to get in nature, and it's all part of just that slowing down."

title: Jeff Foxworthy reveals how 'redneck' insult inspired decades of comedy
summary: Jeff Foxworthy reveals why he brought back his iconic "redneck" jokes after 20 years for his Fox Nation special "The Joke's on Me," streaming now.
story: Foxworthy was able to turn what should have been an insult into a ‘compliment’ by turning it into a ‘badge of honor.’
Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where he came from.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 67-year-old actor and comedian discussed his new stand-up special, "The Joke's on Me," and recalled the time someone called him a "redneck" and how he turned what was meant to be an insult into a compliment.
He explained that "one of the nicest compliments" someone once gave him was commending his ability to turn what "was supposed to be an insult ... into a badge of honor."
DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY
"I said, 'Well, that's cool, because when people get offended, they act like if you gave rednecks a billion dollars, they wouldn't be rednecks,'" he said.

"I said they would still be rednecks. They would just have bigger boats, bigger trucks. I mean, more things to shoot at. They're happy with who they are. And I've always got asked, ‘How do you come up with that?’ And I'm like. There's no research going on. It's my family and my friend group that trust me."
Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up routine. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
Foxworthy first began telling jokes about rednecks in the late '80s, and found them to be successful, so he continued telling them, even closing his 1990 special with one.

He explained that "they were easy to remember" and said they would always "get a laugh." After telling the jokes on stage for a while, he "thought, well people are tired of this" and stopped telling them.
"The last time I did them onstage was during the Blue Collar Comedy Tour" in 2003, he said.
WATCH: Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up.

After more than 20 years of staying away from the jokes, Foxworthy felt like it was time to bring them back. He recalled telling the crowd, "I hadn't done these in 20 years, but I'm thinking about for this special, bringing them back.
"I said that because when I said that if you've ever peed in the pool, the entire audience went, 'You might be a redneck.' And I went, 'Oh, wow, this stuck to people's bones, you know?'" he said.
"And I say, ‘Well, what if I did some to close, if that was my first special, and all these years later, this is my last.’ It kind of seemed like a nice little way to put a bow on it."
Foxworthy brought jokes about rednecks back into his act after realizing they still resonated with his audience. (Gary Gershoff/Getty Images)
He then went back and looked at all the redneck jokes he had written over the years, "and pulled out a bunch of them" to try at his next gig at a comedy club.

"It was like, I never stopped doing them," he said. "It was like going back 35 years, which was really cool for me. It's like one of your babies. You bring it back out and people go, 'Oh, we still love it.'"
WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy explains why he stopped telling 'redneck' jokes

Foxworthy's latest comedy special, "The Joke's on Me" began streaming on Fox Nation in June. Unlike other comedy specials, this one gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the joke-writing process that goes into creating a special.

The comedian told Fox News Digital he was inspired to create the unique special after watching a documentary about the Beatles and realizing that "seeing the process didn't take anything away from the finished product," but rather made it better "because you saw the struggle that went into creating that."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Foxworthy came up with the idea for his new special after watching a documentary about the Beatles. (Getty Images)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
When Fox Nation approached him with the offer to do a stand-up special, he pitched them the behind-the-scenes idea.

"I said, 'But if you're willing to try something different, if you will show me note cards in hand, going into a club on a Tuesday night or a Wednesday night and just throwing these thoughts out.' Because one of the things that still fascinates me after over 40 years about stand-up is I still don't know what people are gonna laugh at," he said.

"You would think after 40 years, I would know. Now, I'll go in there with an idea, 'Oh, this is really funny.' And then nobody laughs. Or I'll have a card where I think this is so stupid, I'm embarrassed to say it, and you throw it out there and everybody's beaten the tables laughing. And you're like, really? And, so, I wanted to show that. And Fox Nation was the first place that ever said, 'OK, we'll do it.'"
Foxworthy has hinted that this could be his last stand-up special but assures fans that doesn't mean he will never perform on a stage again.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Foxworthy hinted this may be his last stand-up special. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images for Beloved Benefit)
He told Fox News Digital he has reached a point in his life where the time he would rather spend with his grandkids or on his tractor.
WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy clears up his comments about retiring from stand-up

"I've been on the road nonstop," he added. "I laugh at my music friends when they say they're on tour. I said, 'Well, tour implies it stops. At some point,' I said, 'I've been on tour since 1984.' It just never stopped. I still love stand-up. I just don't know that I'm willing. And, to be honest, I'm not sure I can do anything any better than this, which just feels like a good place to stop."
Foxworthy's Fox Nation special, "The Joke's On Me," is available to watch now.

title: Brooke Hogan threatens to expose family receipts in 'final warning'
summary: Brooke Hogan threatened to release screenshots after Linda Hogan accused her of tossing the family aside, escalating their public estrangement.
story: HGTV ‘Rock the Block’ contestant Brooke Hogan tells Fox News Digital about her grief and healing journey after her father’s death.
Brooke Hogan is warning her family that she has receipts, and she's prepared to use them.

The 38-year-old daughter of late wrestling legend Hulk Hogan fired back after her mother, Linda Hogan, publicly lamented their yearslong estrangement and accused Brooke of tossing her family aside "like trash."
"This 👌 close to breaking out some screenshots – which are ONE of the many reasons WHY," Brooke wrote over a screenshot of her mother's Facebook post from Aug. 30 shared to her Instagram Story.
BROOKE HOGAN SAYS ‘I COULD HAVE SAVED YOU’ IN HAUNTING REGRET AFTER HULK HOGAN’S DEATH
Brooke Hogan threatened to bring out the "receipts" as her bitter family feud with mother Linda Hogan erupted again. (Brooke Hogan Oleksy/Instagram )
"I don't take CONSTANTLY dragging my name through the mud lightly," she continued.
"The selective amnesia isn't gonna work."
Brooke ended the message with two words: "Final warning."
The latest flare-up came after Linda shared old family photos on Facebook while expressing her frustration over her fractured relationship with her daughter.
"I posted these wonderful photos of Brooke my daughter with me and my ex-husband her father and my mom and dad and really .. the whole family ! Brooke is loved," Linda wrote.
"We feel hurt every day that she just tosses us aside .... like trash," she continued. "I want to make sure she remembers how it really was .. and can really see how much she was adored and loved."
Brooke's response suggested she remembers their family history differently and is prepared to make private communications public if the criticism continues.
The mother and daughter's latest exchange is another chapter in a fractured family that has played out publicly for years.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Brooke Hogan with her brother, Nick Hogan, and parents Hulk Hogan and Linda Hogan. (Michael Loccisano/FilmMagic)
Brooke first became famous alongside her parents, Hulk and Linda, and younger brother, Nick Hogan, on the VH1 reality series "Hogan Knows Best," which premiered in 2005.
The show followed the wrestling superstar and his family while also documenting Brooke's budding music career and her father's protective approach to his teenage daughter.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
The family dynamic changed dramatically after Linda filed for divorce from Hulk in 2007 after more than two decades of marriage. Their divorce was finalized in 2009.
Years later, Brooke became estranged from both parents, but she has made clear that her reasons for cutting contact with her mother were separate from the issues she had with her father.
Brooke addressed the family rift directly in a lengthy Instagram statement on March 27, 2025, insisting she had not chosen one parent over the other.

"No contact with my mom has nothing to do with my dad, and no contact with my father has nothing to do with my mother," Brooke wrote. "I have completely separate reasons for going no contact with each of my parents."
HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED
In the same statement, Brooke made serious allegations about her childhood and family relationships.

"I have been EXTREMELY verbally and mentally abused since childhood," she alleged. "Sadly, it would frequently turn physical. And sometimes it's not by the person you would assume, abuse comes in all shapes and sizes."
Brooke did not identify a specific person in that portion of her statement.
The Hogan family at the 2004 Radio Music Awards in Las Vegas in October 2004. (Frank Micelotta/Getty Images)
She also claimed she had been put in the position of publicly defending behavior within her family before eventually questioning what she had been told.
"I've been asked to defend poor behavior to the public and have done so out of love. Only to find I was misinformed, manipulated, and lied to," she wrote.
"I longed for a normal family, but it never came to fruition. I've repeatedly held my hand out to help them, only to have them pull me into the darkness with them.
"I've set boundaries that were not respected, which turned into a 'no contact' situation."
Her comments came after Linda publicly discussed the family's troubles in March 2025, reigniting attention around their strained relationship.
The conflict marked a dramatic departure from the image viewers were introduced to two decades earlier on "Hogan Knows Best."
Brooke was a teenager when the series premiered, with the show following her budding music career, dating life and her father's famously protective parenting.
WWE LEGEND HULK HOGAN'S DEATH REPORT RELEASED
Brooke previously told Fox News Digital that, despite her strained relationship with her father, she loved him. (Acey Harper/Getty Images)
In the years that followed, the family relationships viewers once watched on television became increasingly strained, with some of those disputes eventually playing out in public.
Her relationship with her father received renewed attention after his death on July 24, 2025.
Hulk, born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 after being hospitalized for cardiac arrest.
Hulk was survived by Brooke and Nick, whom he shared with Linda, as well as his wife, Sky Daily.
Despite being estranged from her father when he died, Brooke made clear in an April interview with Fox News Digital that her love for him had never disappeared.

"I’m honest with him now, and I talk to him all the time, even if that seems like I’m a cuckoo bird," she told Fox News Digital. "If he showed up today, I would just be like, ‘I love you so much, and I wish you would have just let me in.’"
Brooke also offered rare insight into why their relationship had become strained before his death.
Brooke said that she wanted to "save" her father before his death. (John Parra/WireImage)

"[It's] tough because, obviously, my dad and I weren't really speaking prior to his death — not because I didn't love him. … It's that he had become a little bit calloused in the direction he was going in his life and the people he was surrounding himself with," she said.

"I am the daughter that wanted to save him. And it's kind of, like, you can try to save somebody and if they don't want to be saved … it's a tough position to be in."
Her comments to Fox News Digital echoed what Brooke had emphasized in her March 2025 statement. Distancing herself from her father did not mean she had sided with her mother or vice versa.

title: Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan among stars who left fame behind before returning to Hollywood
summary: From Rick Moranis to Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan, these Hollywood stars walked away from fame and made remarkable comebacks years later on screen.
story: Actor Jonathan Bennett tells Fox News Digital he’s excited about his ‘Mean Girls’ co-star Lindsay Lohan’s return to acting and discusses co-hosting ChristmasCon with Lacey Chabert.
Rick Moranis is stepping back into the spotlight after decades away from Hollywood, joining a growing list of stars who left fame behind and later returned.
The 73-year-old actor is taking on his first live-action part in nearly 30 years after walking away from the entertainment industry at the height of his career after a family tragedy.
Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet in "Spaceballs: The New One," the long-awaited sequel to Mel Brooks' 1987 cult classic science-fiction comedy movie, "Spaceballs."
'DEADPOOL' STAR ROB DELANEY REVEALS HOW LOSING 2-YEAR-OLD SON CHANGED HIS APPROACH TO FAME

Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan disappeared from Hollywood before making triumphant returns years later. (David Becker/Getty Images for CinemaCon; Dave Benett/WireImage; Jeff Spicer/Getty Images)

In July, Moranis made a rare public appearance to promote the sequel at San Diego Comic-Con, where he received a standing ovation when he appeared on stage wearing his character's signature massive black helmet. Moranis participated in a panel discussion alongside co-stars Daphne Zuniga, Josh Gad, Keke Palmer and Lewis Pullman, as well as director Josh Greenbaum and screenwriters Benji Samit and Dan Hernandez.
Zuniga is reprising her role as Princess Vespa, while other original stars who returned for the sequel include George Wyner as Colonel Sandurz, Bill Pullman as Lone Starr and Brooks as Yogurt.
During the panel, Moranis revealed what finally brought him back in front of the camera after his decades-long hiatus.
Moranis made a surprise appearance at the "Spaceballs: The New One" panel at Comic-Con International: San Diego in July. (Variety via Getty Images)

"This came along right at the right time, and I started talking to these folks and hearing who was going to be in it," Moranis said, via People. "I spoke to Josh Greenbaum, and I heard that Bill Pullman was coming back, and that Lewis was going to be in it too. And it just felt like this is it. It’s time and — yes. I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made."

Moranis became one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in the 1980s and 1990s after starring in a string of hit movies, including "Spaceballs," "Ghostbusters," "Little Shop of Horrors," "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," "Parenthood," "My Blue Heaven" and "The Flintstones."

However, after his wife, costume designer Ann Belsky, died in 1991 after a battle with breast cancer, Moranis stepped away from show business to focus on raising their two children, daughter Rachel and son Mitchell. He last appeared on-screen in 1997's "Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves," the third installment in the "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" movie series.
Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet. (Alamy)
During a 2015 interview with the Hollywood Reporter, Moranis reflected on his decision to prioritize his family over his career.

"I was working with really interesting people, wonderful people," he said. "I went from that to being at home with a couple of little kids, which is a very different lifestyle. But it was important to me. I have absolutely no regrets whatsoever. My life is wonderful."
Moranis also clarified that he had not officially retired from acting, telling the outlet, "I took a break, which turned into a longer break."

"But I’m interested in anything that I would find interesting," he continued. "I still get the occasional query about a film or television role and as soon as one comes along that piques my interest, I'll probably do it.
MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE
"I’m happy with the things I said yes to, and I’m very happy with the many things I’ve said no to," Moranis added. "Yes, I am picky, and I’ll continue to be picky. Picky has worked for me."
One of Rick Moranis' final on-screen roles was in "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," in 1989. (AJ Pics/Alamy Stock Photo)

Though Moranis left live-action films behind for many years, he continued working occasionally as a voice actor. He first dipped his toe back into the movie business in 2001, voicing two characters in "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer & the Island of Misfit Toys." Some of his other voice-acting gigs include "Brother Bear," "The Animated Adventures of Bob & Doug McKenzie" and the voice of Dark Helmet in "The Goldbergs."

During his appearance at Comic-Con, Moranis once again set the record straight regarding the perception that he had retired as he revealed that he and Brooks had long discussed making a follow-up to "Spaceballs."
"Actually, I started talking to Mel about the sequel in 1989," he said. "We kept talking about it.
"I really wasn’t retired; I was just negotiating."
STOCKARD CHANNING HITS FIRST RED CARPET IN 2 YEARS AFTER SAYING SHE'S A 'RECLUSE'

While Moranis’ return has drawn renewed attention due to his decades-long absence, other stars have also taken long breaks from Hollywood before making high-profile comebacks. Here's a look at several celebrities who stepped away from the spotlight for years before finding their way back to the screen.
Cameron Diaz
Cameron Diaz returned to Hollywood after stepping away from acting in 2014. (Getty Images)
Cameron Diaz was one of Hollywood’s most bankable stars when she quietly stepped away from acting in 2014.

Diaz made her breakthrough in 1994's "The Mask" and went on to star in a series of hit films, including "There’s Something About Mary," "My Best Friend's Wedding," "Charlie's Angels," "My Sister's Keeper," "Shrek" and "The Other Woman," among others.
After starring in 2014's "Annie," Diaz walked away from show business to focus on building a life with husband Benji Madden.

"It felt like the right thing for me to reclaim my own life, and I just really didn't care about anything else," the actress said during a 2025 appearance at Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit, according to E! News.

"Nobody's opinion, nobody's success, no one's offer, no one's anything could change my mind about my decision of taking care of myself and building the life that I really wanted to have. I think it really comes to what are you passionate about? For me, it was to build my family."
During her break, Diaz welcomed daughter Raddix, 6, and son Cardinal, 2, with Madden and launched her Avaline wine brand. The couple's third child, son Nautus, was born in May.

After a decade away from movies, Diaz returned to the screen in Netflix’s 2025 action comedy "Back in Action," starring opposite Jamie Foxx. She has since lined up other projects, including Netflix’s "Bad Day," Apple TV+’s "Outcome" and "Shrek 5," in which she will reprise her voice role as Princess Fiona.
Lindsay Lohan
Lindsay Lohan mounted a comeback years after fleeing Hollywood for Dubai. (Todd Owyoung/NBC via Getty Images)
Lindsay Lohan’s comeback followed years of intense public scrutiny and a long stretch away from major studio films.
Lohan became one of Hollywood’s biggest young stars after breaking out in "The Parent Trap" and later leading hits including "Freaky Friday," "Mean Girls" and "Herbie: Fully Loaded."

However, Lohan's promising career was derailed by multiple box-office flops and a string of highly-publicized legal problems and substance abuse issues. After years of tabloid attention and personal struggles, Lohan left the United States in 2014 and eventually relocated full-time to Dubai, spending much of the next decade outside the Hollywood spotlight. She told Emirates Woman in 2018 that moving to Dubai afforded her "a fresh start."

Lohan began rebuilding her acting career with Netflix’s 2022 holiday movie "Falling for Christmas," followed by more streaming projects and a major return to one of her signature roles in "Freakier Friday."

During a 2025 interview with The Sunday Times, Lohan said she stepped away because she had lost her excitement for making movies and wanted "a more private life, a real life," before returning once she felt "that itch again."
Lohan will next be seen in Hulu’s "Count My Lies," a limited series in which she stars opposite Shailene Woodley and Kit Harington.
Ke Huy Quan
Ke Huy Quan's comeback culminated in a Best Supporting Actor Oscar win. (Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Image)
Ke Huy Quan’s Hollywood disappearance ended with one of the industry’s most celebrated comeback stories.

Quan became a child star after playing Short Round opposite Harrison Ford in 1984’s "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom" and Data in 1985’s "The Goonies." However, Ke only landed a few minor TV and film roles after his early fame and found himself being offered stereotypical parts geared toward Asians.

During a 2023 interview with People, Quan said he made the "very difficult decision" to walk away from acting in the early 2000s. He then spent years working behind the camera as a stunt coordinator and assistant director.
However, he recalled that, after seeing 2018’s "Crazy Rich Asians," he was inspired to revisit his first love.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"I was happy working behind the camera, but I had serious FOMO (fear of missing out)," Ke told the outlet. "I wanted to be up there with my fellow Asian actors."

After roughly two decades away from acting, Quan returned in 2022’s "Everything Everywhere All at Once," a role that earned him the Academy Award for best supporting actor. In his emotional Oscars speech, Quan reflected on his unlikely journey, saying, "Dreams are something you have to believe in. I almost gave up on mine."
Daniel Day-Lewis
Daniel Day-Lewis returned to Hollywood to team up with his son Ronan for 2025's "Anemone." (Jason Merritt/WireImage)
Daniel Day-Lewis has stepped away from Hollywood more than once, but his latest return marked the end of what many believed was a permanent retirement.

Known for his intensely selective approach to roles, Day-Lewis has previously taken long breaks throughout his career. After starring in 1997’s "The Boxer," Day-Lewis retreated from acting and spent several years in Italy learning shoemaking before returning in Martin Scorsese’s 2002 film, "Gangs of New York."

The three-time Oscar winner announced he was retiring from acting after starring in 2017’s "Phantom Thread." At the time, his representative said, "Daniel Day-Lewis will no longer be working as an actor. He is immensely grateful to all of his collaborators and audiences over the many years. This is a private decision and neither he nor his representatives will make any further comment on this subject."
Eight years later, his son, Ronan Day-Lewis, persuaded him to co-write and star in the 2025 drama "Anemone."
Day-Lewis later pushed back on the idea that he ever meant to permanently retire.

In a 2025 Rolling Stone interview, Day-Lewis said he "never intended to retire, really" and called his earlier retirement announcement "grandiose gibberish." He explained that he still loved the work but struggled with the lifestyle around filmmaking and felt "hollowed out" after "Phantom Thread."

He said returning for "Anemone" was largely about working with Ronan, who directed the film. Day-Lewis said that collaboration brought the spark back, saying, "Working with Ro, that furnace just lit up."
Renée Zellweger
Renee Zellweger took a six-year break from acting. (Getty Images)
Renée Zellweger stepped away from Hollywood after years of working at a relentless pace.

Zellweger became one of the most prominent actresses of the late 1990s and 2000s with roles in the hit movies "Jerry Maguire," "Bridget Jones’s Diary," "Chicago," "Cold Mountain" and "Cinderella Man." But after 2010’s "My Own Love Song," Zellweger took a six-year break from acting.
During a 2025 interview with British Vogue, Zellweger explained why she decided to pause her career.

"I was sick of the sound of my own voice. When I was working, I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, listen to you. Are you sad again, Renée? Oh, is this your mad voice?’ It was a regurgitation of the same emotional experiences," she said.
Zellweger told the outlet that her hiatus from acting enabled her to pursue other projects and embrace a healthier lifestyle.

"I wrote music and studied international law," she said. "I built a house, rescued a pair of older doggies, created a partnership that led to a production company, advocated for and fundraised with a sick friend and spent a lot of time with family and godchildren and driving across the country with the dogs. I got healthy."

Zellweger returned in 2016 with the hit sequel "Bridget Jones’s Baby." She went on to earn some of the strongest reviews of her career for playing Judy Garland in 2019’s "Judy," and her performance earned her the Academy Award for best actress. Zellweger previously won the best supporting actress Oscar for her performance in "Cold Mountain."
Macaulay Culkin
Macaulay Culkin stepped away from acting as a teenager after childhood fame. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic)
Macaulay Culkin walked away from Hollywood after becoming one of the most famous child stars in the world.

Culkin shot to superstardom as Kevin McCallister in 1990’s "Home Alone" and its 1992 sequel, "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York." He went on to star in hit films, including "My Girl," "The Good Son" and "Richie Rich."

After filming "Richie Rich," Culkin stepped away from acting, later explaining that he wanted to attend school, date and spend time with people his own age.

He returned nine years later with "Party Monster" and has continued accepting occasional projects on his own terms, including roles in "Saved!," "American Horror Story: Double Feature" and "The Righteous Gemstones."
Pamela Anderson
Pamela Anderson embraced a quieter lifestyle before her career reinvention. (Getty Images)
Pamela Anderson’s return to the spotlight has become one of Hollywood’s more unexpected late-career reinventions.

Anderson became a global sex symbol in the 1990s through "Baywatch," Playboy and years of tabloid attention that often overshadowed her acting ambitions. After decades of being defined by her image and personal life, she retreated to Vancouver Island, embraced a quieter lifestyle and began reassessing the public persona that had followed her for much of her career.

Her comeback began with a wave of projects that allowed her to reclaim her own story, including the 2023 Netflix documentary "Pamela, a Love Story" and her memoir, "Love, Pamela."
She made her Broadway debut in "Chicago" in 2022 and earned some of the strongest reviews of her career for "The Last Showgirl," along with Golden Globe and SAG nominations.

title: Trump pardons Jay-Z associate Emory Jones after federal drug conviction
summary: Alice Marie Johnson revealed Trump granted clemency to 30 individuals, including Emory Jones, a Roc Nation executive and Jay-Z's longtime associate.
story: Jon Bon Jovi and Jay-Z said their hellos on the field ahead of the 2026 Super Bowl.
Emory Jones, longtime friend and business associate of Jay-Z, has been granted a pardon from President Donald Trump.

Jones, an executive with Jay-Z's Roc Nation, was sentenced to nearly 16 years in 2000 on federal drug charges. Thanks in part to a letter from the hip-hop mogul, his sentence was reduced by 37 months, but now Trump has given him a completely clean slate.

The news was shared this week by Alice Marie Johnson, who was pardoned by Trump in 2020 after being sentenced to life in prison on a nonviolent drug charge in 1996. She now works with the White House as the "pardon czar."
JELLY ROLL GRANTED PARDON BY TENNESSEE GOVERNOR IN CHRISTMAS SEASON CLEMENCY DECISION
Trump pardoned 30 individuals Sept. 3, including Jay-Z's friend and business associate, Emory Jones. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images; Kevork S. Djansezian/Getty Images)

"Yesterday was a powerful day for second chances," Johnson wrote on Instagram. "I am deeply grateful to President @realdonaldtrump for granting clemency and pardons to 30 deserving individuals whose cases we carefully reviewed and brought forward — and to the White House Counsel team, led by Will Scharf, for the hard work behind these decisions.

"Among them is Emory Jones, who served nearly 16 years in federal prison and came home determined to build a different life. Today he is an entrepreneur and creative leader whose journey reminds us how much people can grow — and how much good they can still do."
TODD CHRISLEY RECALLS EMOTIONAL PHONE CALL WITH DAUGHTER SAVANNAH AFTER CONTROVERSIAL TRUMP PARDON
In 1999, Jones pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiracy to distribute cocaine. The following year, he was sentenced to 188 months, nearly 16 years, in prison, with five years supervised release.
Jones was originally sentenced to 188 months in prison before his sentence was reduced to 151 months. (Getty Images for Fanatics)
Jones' legal team submitted a request for a reduction of his sentence in 2009, and, as part of their request, it submitted a series of letters from people familiar with Jones, including Jay-Z.

In a letter to the judge, Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, wrote that he'd be offering Jones an executive assistant job with Roc Apparel Group upon his release, with a starting salary of $50,000.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Jay-Z, photographed with wife Beyoncé, wrote a letter to the judge in 2009 in attempt to get Jones' sentence reduced. (Mike Coppola/Getty Images)

"As you might expect, this position needs to be filled as soon as possible," he wrote. "It is my strong desire to have Mr. Jones fill this position. I have known Mr. Jones for 15 years. I believe his attributes, including intelligence, interpersonal skills and solid work ethic will be a significant asset for my organization."

In another letter, Jones wrote about his conviction, saying, "Of all the excuses that I could have attributed my demise to, I chose not to use a single one. Excuses are tools of the incompetent and only build monuments to nothingness."

He also included mention of his support system, including Jay-Z, writing, "When a person or people make sacrifices and devote themselves to supporting you through the adversity of incarceration, you owe them.
"Nothing monetary because you can't put a price on love and support. However, you do owe them the privilege and opportunity to see you do something extremely positive with your life."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Jones still works with Jay-Z with his Roc Nation brand. (Getty Images)
Jones was resentenced to 151 months, still with five years supervised release, shaving 37 months off of his original sentence.

Today, he's the head of lifestyle at Roc Nation, and he has an executive role in fashion brand Paper Planes, which he and Jay-Z founded in 2014.
