title: 4 family members flying from Bahamas to Florida in small plane go missing, with Coast Guard joining search
summary: Four Florida family members remain missing on Tuesday after their plane vanished while traveling home from the Bahamas over Labor Day weekend.
story: The 'Fox & Friends' hosts review dramatic footage of 23-year-old pilot Faith Tenkley surviving an emergency water landing off the coast of Boca Raton, Florida, on August 22. Tenkley successfully guides her single-engine aircraft away from beachgoers and paddleboarders before swimming safely to shore, earning praise from local authorities for her quick and professional decision-making.
The U.S. Coast Guard has joined the search for a plane carrying four Florida family members that authorities in the Bahamas believe "crash-landed" in the ocean after departing from Great Harbour Cay.

Pilot Mario Lamar, 80, his wife Lili, 79, and two of their grandchildren, Sofia Sosa, 28, and Christian Sosa, 22, were identified by family as those on board the PA-34 Piper five-seater aircraft that was heading to Opa-locka, Florida, according to the Miami Herald.

"Please help," Silvia Larrieu, the niece of the couple, told the newspaper. "I ask anybody out there, if you can help with search and rescue efforts, we would greatly appreciate it. We need to bring them home."

Larrieu said the four were coming home to Florida after visiting a vacation property in Great Harbour Cay over Labor Day weekend and that "they’ve spent their whole life going there." Data from the website FlightAware showed the plane descended from 10,000 feet to 3,700 feet in about three minutes before vanishing from radar.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY
Great Harbour Cay in the Bahamas is seen from an airplane during a flight from Spain to the Caribbean. (NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Larrieu told the Miami Herald that Mario Lamar had years of experience as a pilot and always kept the aircraft in "pristine" shape.

U.S. Coast Guard Southeast said Monday it was assisting authorities in the Bahamas "following a report of a downed aircraft with four souls on board approx 15 mi off Andros Island," with a Coast Guard HC-144 Ocean Sentry airplane joining the search.
The Royal Bahamas Police Force said it received a report around 2:20 p.m. on Monday "that an aircraft may have gone down in the waters off Red Bays."
COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY ONBOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE

A U.S. Coast Guard HC-144 Ocean Sentry medium-range surveillance plane from Air Station Cape Cod flies over the Atlantic Ocean in Newport, R.I., on April 4, 2026. One of these planes has joined the search for the missing aircraft off the coast of the Bahamas. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

It added that air traffic control "confirmed that a PA-34 Piper five-seater aircraft, bearing tail number N212ML, departed Great Harbour Cay at approximately 11:12 a.m., en route to Opa-locka, Florida."
"Air traffic control subsequently lost contact with the aircraft approximately 13 miles west of Andros Island," the Royal Bahamas Police Force said.
A U.S. Coast Guard aircraft is seen at Opa Locka Executive Airport in Opa Locka, Fla., on July 17, 2021. (REUTERS)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The Bahamas Air Sea Rescue Association (BASRA) advised that the United States Coast Guard had attempted to search the area for the missing aircraft," police also said. "However, due to inclement weather, the search was postponed until conditions became favorable."
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Massive fire engulfs apartment complex under construction, forces evacuations in South Bend
summary: A massive construction fire engulfed the Stadium Flats apartments in South Bend, Indiana, forcing emergency evacuation of neighboring residents.
story: The fire erupted just after midnight at the Stadium Flats apartment development in South Bend, Indiana, near the training facility for the South Bend Cubs, the city's minor league baseball team. (Credit: @goonie52832 via Storyful)

A massive fire early Tuesday morning tore through an apartment complex under construction in South Bend, Indiana, forcing residents of a neighboring building to evacuate, according to local officials.
The South Bend Fire Department said the fire began just after midnight at the Stadium Flats apartments near S. Lafayette & W. South Street.
Fire crews arrived to a scene of towering flames and billowing smoke after receiving reports that the blaze had engulfed both the building under construction and a crane.
CRANE ARM COLLAPSES INTO MIAMI CONDO ROOFTOP POOL AREA AS WORKERS CLING TO DANGLING STRUCTURE

A massive fire engulfs the Stadium Flats apartment complex in South Bend, Indiana, on Sept. 8, 2026. The building was under construction and would have added dozens of affordable housing units to the city. (South Bend Fire Department)
Despite the fire producing "a significant amount of embers and debris," firefighters were able to keep it from spreading to the neighboring Diamond View Apartments.

Residents of the Diamond View Apartments were evacuated during the fire, with officials saying the heat damaged several windows on the building's top floor. The building has 60 units of affordable housing, according to a report last year in the South Bend Tribune.
Crews from the South Bend Fire Department arrived to the scene shortly after midnight on Sept. 8, 2026. (South Bend Fire Department)
MASSIVE CHEMICAL FIRE ERUPTS AT ELECTRICAL TRANSFORMER PLANT IN MISSISSIPPI, FORCING EVACUATION
The Stadium Flats building was set to introduce 92 additional affordable units to downtown South Bend. Before the fire, construction was expected to be completed by spring 2027.

Both buildings are near the training facility for the South Bend Cubs, the city's minor league baseball team. Firefighters were able to stop the blaze from spreading to the 17,000-square-foot complex, which is right next to the baseball stadium.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation, officials said. No injuries or fatalities were reported. (South Bend Fire Department)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Officials said the cause of the fire remains under investigation. No injuries or deaths were reported.
The fire occurred a little over two miles from the University of Notre Dame's campus.

title: Texas education board approves controversial curriculum changes tying 'radical Islam' to 9/11 attacks
summary: The Texas Board of Education gave final approval to controversial social studies changes impacting how students learn about Islam and Christianity.
story: Rep. Mike Lawler joins 'Saturday in America' to react to reports that a local administration is building a network of social media influencers to promote its agenda. Lawler discusses the impact of these policies on New York business owners and outlines his bipartisan legislation to mandate 9/11 historical curriculum in classrooms nationwide.

The Texas Board of Education gave final approval to changes to the state's high school social studies curriculum, a controversial move that will impact how students are taught about Islam and Christianity.

The amended social studies curriculum, which covers U.S. history, government and world geography, comes after dozens of people gave public testimony, with most expressing their opposition to the finalized version.
The board approved language asserting that "radical Islam" motivated the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks rather than taking a more narrow focus on the terrorist groups involved in the attack.

The material also requires students to study early Islam through Prophet Muhammad's "brutal military campaigns against Jewish and Christian tribes," the "normalization of slavery" and the taking of female captives as "harem slaves."
NBA CHAMPION JOSH HART CELEBRATES TEXAS BOARD OF EDUCATION'S VOTE TO MAKE BIBLE PASSAGES REQUIRED READING
The Texas Board of Education gave final approval to changes to the state's high school social studies curriculum. (iStock)
Several Democratic State Board of Education members pushed back against the wording, but the Republican-majority board still approved that section and the other changes on Friday.
Muslim groups and students, as well as multiple curriculum experts, also spoke out against the new changes.

"I feel attacked, as if my religion doesn’t belong," Habiiba Quresh, a 15-year-old Muslim student, told the board, according to The Texas Tribune. "I shouldn't have to defend my religion in the middle of history class because of one sentence someone on this board wrote."
At least three of the board-appointed curriculum experts also warned against the new language.
TED CRUZ, CONSERVATIVES RESPOND AFTER TALARICO CRITICIZES BIBLE-RELATED EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS AS 'PROPAGANDA'

The board approved language asserting that "radical Islam" motivated the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks rather than taking a more narrow focus on the terrorist groups involved in the attack. (Antonio Perez/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Andrea Hutchison, a social studies curriculum coordinator for Prosper ISD, argued the material did not "hold up to close historical scrutiny," according to the outlet. Robert Koons, a philosophy professor at UT-Austin, said most nonreligious scholars find the source of the claims "not very reliable," adding that he would warn against including material that is "not based on well-established secular sources."

The Texas chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations said the board’s decision to "single out and denigrate Islam, minimize the brutal realities of slavery and segregation, and entirely erase Palestinian history is an affront to our system of education and the First Amendment."

"No credible scholar of history validates the bigoted caricatures of Islam this curriculum teaches," CAIR Texas and CAIR Action Texas said in a joint statement. "Even the board’s own appointed experts warned it doesn’t hold up to historical scrutiny, yet the board voted against removing it. Texas students of every background deserve an education that tells the truth about their history and their neighbors’ history, not propaganda that teaches them to see each other as threats or erases them from the story altogether."
Muslim groups and students, as well as multiple curriculum experts, spoke out against the new changes. (Jay Janner/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images)

State Board of Education Chair Aaron Kinsey pushed back on criticism of the revised standards, saying opponents had "sensationalize[d] all these topics and [made] them seem more divisive than they actually are." He added that board members "worked through, democratically, how to make those choices on behalf of our constituents" and said he believed they "did an exceptional job overall."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
But Republican school board member Julie Pickren boasted about the material's final approval, according to Fox 7.

"This social studies law that got us here, I've been working on for over 10 years with the House and the Senate, the Texas House and Texas Senate ... and so this is such a huge accomplishment; this vote kind of bookends 12 years of life's work," Pickren said.
The approved curriculum is expected to be phased into classrooms during the 2030-31 school year.

title: Climber dies in fatal fall on Colorado 14er south of Aspen
summary: A 21-member rescue team was dispatched to the remote mountain after nearby hikers witnessed the climber fall and officials determined the injuries were not survivable.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Officials in Colorado said a climber suffered a fatal fall Sunday after scaling a towering peak south of Aspen.
The tragic incident occurred on Castle Peak, which reaches a steep elevation of 14,272 feet in the Elk Mountains, according to Mountain Rescue Aspen.
Responders said rescue team members reached the climber by 4 p.m. after the Gunnison County Sheriff's Office was notified of a fallen climber.
However, officials "determined the individual had sustained injuries that were not survivable."
NORTH CAROLINA CLIMBER AIRLIFTED AFTER PLUNGING 20 FEET DOWN GORGE, SUSTAINING SERIOUS INJURIES
Responders reached the climber by 4 p.m. but determined the injuries could not be survived. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)
The fall was apparently witnessed by nearby hikers, including Rebecca Rees, who recounted the incident in a statement posted to Facebook.
"Unfortunately, we witnessed the event. It has been an extremely sad and terrible afternoon for all involved. He did not survive," she said.
Rees said a bystander, identified as Robert, even scrambled toward the climber immediately after the fall, putting himself at risk in case there was still a chance of survival.
She added that the victim ultimately "wasn’t alone" in his final moments.
NOVICE CLIMBER SURVIVES 1,500-FOOT DROP ON CALIFORNIA'S MOUNT SHASTA AFTER HELICOPTER RESCUE DELAYED BY CLOUDS
Nearby hikers reportedly witnessed the fall at Castle Peak, south of Aspen. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)
Rees said the rescue crew responded at a commendable speed. Despite the remote location, helicopter and ground teams reportedly reached nearly 13,000 feet in under two hours on a holiday weekend.
According to Mountain Rescue Aspen, officials used off-highway vehicles and helicopters to reach the remote area.
After a helicopter located the fallen climber, it returned to Aspen to pick up additional rescue personnel before taking them to the high-elevation area near the peak.
MOUNTAIN CLIMBER SURVIVES TERRIFYING 500-FOOT FALL IN CALIFORNIA'S SIERRA NEVADA, NIGHT STRANDED ON LEDGE
Officials said the climber was recovered from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)
A total of 21 rescue members were sent into the field, and officials safely recovered and evacuated the deceased climber from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m.
Rees said the responders showed extraordinary compassion throughout the recovery effort.
The rescue operation unfolded at elevations approaching 13,000 feet. (Mountain Rescue Aspen)

"The response of search and rescue, the sheriff, and the coroner all made us feel like every single person matters. This young man had a story and we all care," she said.

title: US forces sink narco-refueling station linked to Ecuadorian cartel in Pacific: SOUTHCOM
summary: U.S. forces sank a Los Choneros refueling vessel in the Eastern Pacific after SOUTHCOM said it supported at-sea drug trafficking operations.
story: The vessel was involved with Los Choneros, an Ecuadorian organized crime syndicate, U.S. Southern Command said (Credit: X @Southcom).
U.S. forces on Monday sank a floating refueling vessel used by an Ecuadorian organized crime ring, officials said.

Forces with Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTFWH) interdicted the refueling vessel used for "at-sea drug trafficking operations" in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said.
"JTF-WHEM continues to conduct precise and professional operations to dismantle the logistical networks fueling narco-trafficking in the Western Hemisphere," a SOUTHCOM post on X states.
The vessel was involved with the Los Choneros narco-terrorist organization, SOUTHCOM said. The people aboard were removed and will be handed over to Ecuadorian authorities.
NEWLY UNCLASSIFIED PENTAGON IMAGES SHOW SUSPECTED DRUG BOATS AS OFFICIAL ISSUES DEADLY WARNING
U.S. Forces on Monday sank a refueling vessel used by Los Choneros, an Ecuadorian organized crime ring, in the Eastern Pacific Ocean. (U.S. Southern Command)
Once the boat was cleared, U.S. forces sank it.
JTFWH was activated by SOUTHCOM in August to counter threats, strengthen regional security, and respond to crises in the Western Hemisphere.
The Trump administration has prioritized targeting suspected drug-smuggling vessels bound for the United States.
US KILLS TWO 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN STRIKE 2 MONTHS SINCE LAST ANNOUNCED ANTI-'NARCO-TRAFFICKING' ATTACK
U.S. forces have launched dozens of strikes targeting such boats under the administration's anti-drug campaign.

Last week, the cartel was designated by the State Department as a foreign terrorist organization. Its members have attacked and threatened public officials and their families, security personnel, judges, prosecutors, and journalists in Ecuador, the agency said.

"Their ultimate goal is to control drug trafficking routes through Ecuador by terrorizing and inflicting brutal violence on the Ecuadorian people," said State Department deputy spokesperson Thomas Pigott.

In July, U.S. and Ecuadorian authorities cooperated to extradite Los Choneros leader Fito Macias, who was the first Ecuadorian citizen extradited from Ecuador to face justice in the U.S.

title: Jimmy John's employee accused of opening fire on car, shooting 14-year-old girl in leg: police
summary: Police say that a dispute at a St. Louis Jimmy John's escalated into gunfire, leaving a 14-year-old girl wounded and an employee facing felony charges.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A dispute that began at a Jimmy John's restaurant in St. Louis ended with a 14-year-old girl shot in the leg and a restaurant employee facing charges for allegedly opening fire on a vehicle carrying the teen, according to police and court records.

The teenage girl was struck shortly before 6 p.m. Saturday near the intersection of Vandeventer and Laclede avenues and was taken to a local hospital, where she was listed in stable condition, the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department said in a statement on X.
Court documents identified the alleged shooter as 27-year-old Adam White, whom police say was an employee at the Jimmy John's where the confrontation began.
MISSOURI ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER HIDDEN VIDEO FOUND ON WIFE'S PHONE, INVESTIGATORS SAY
Police said the shooting stemmed from a dispute involving the teenage girl's mother and "several individuals" associated with the Jimmy John's in the 3800 block of Laclede. (Google Maps)
White is charged with first-degree assault, armed criminal action, unlawful use of a weapon, first-degree child endangerment, among other felony offenses.
In their statement, police said the shooting stemmed from a dispute involving the teenage girl's mother and "several individuals" associated with the Jimmy John's in the 3800 block of Laclede.

"A preliminary investigation indicates the shooting followed a disagreement involving the girl’s mother and several individuals associated with the Jimmy John’s in the 3800 block of Laclede. The mother’s connection to the restaurant remains under investigation," the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department said.
According to investigators, the girl's mother's boyfriend later arrived at the restaurant with the 14-year-old. The confrontation escalated, and gunfire erupted.
GOP CANDIDATE GETS BUSTED ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO PLANT DRUGS ON HIS POLITICAL RIVAL
Court documents identified the alleged shooter as 27-year-old Adam White. (City of St. Louis)
Court documents allege that White got into a verbal argument with a former employee, which continued into the parking lot.
Police say the former employee, her boyfriend and her juvenile daughter then got into a vehicle.
As the vehicle drove away, White allegedly fired multiple rounds into its rear, striking the teenage girl in the left leg.
"As they drove off, the defendant fired multiple rounds into the rear of the vehicle. Victim 3, the juvenile, was struck by one of the bullets in her left leg," court documents state.
Investigators said they found ballistic damage to the trunk of the vehicle.
US MARSHALS SURVIVE DECK COLLAPSE WHILE SERVING WARRANT AT SEX OFFENDER'S HOME
According to court documents, White initially fled the scene but later returned and was taken into custody. (Karl Merton Ferron/The Baltimore Sun/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

According to court documents, White initially fled the scene but later returned and was taken into custody. After being advised of his Miranda rights, White allegedly admitted firing at the vehicle and told detectives he had left the gun at his home.
A judge ordered White held without bond pending trial.
Jimmy John's and the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

title: Prosecutors drop Khalid Sheikh Mohammed confession appeal to protect 2028 trial for alleged 9/11 mastermind
summary: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed's 2007 confession was thrown out over "severe coercion," but prosecutors won't appeal to protect the June 2028 trial date.
story: Former assistant U.S. attorney Andy McCarthy analyzes evidentiary obstacles in prosecuting 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, judicial rulings on mail-in ballots as North Carolina begins distribution and the prosecution's strategy following an 11-1 jury deadlock in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial.

Military prosecutors will move ahead with the trial against the mastermind of the Sept. 11 attacks without a key confession, a decision made to avoid further delays in the long-awaited proceedings scheduled for 2028.
The federal government has decided not to appeal a recent ruling by a military judge that threw out statements made by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed in 2007.
The decision means Mohammed's statements to the FBI cannot be used at trial.

"An appeal could jeopardize the hard-earned June 5, 2028, trial date," the prosecution team's liaison to victims wrote in a letter Friday — a week before the 25th anniversary of the attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people, sources familiar with the matter told The New York Post.
NEW EVIDENCE IN LOCKERBIE PAN AM FLIGHT 103 BOMBING CASE PUSHES FEDERAL JUDGE TO POSTPONE TRIAL
Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks, has been held at Guantánamo Bay since 2003. (AP)

Appeals can take years to resolve, an outcome military prosecutors want to avoid given the series of delays that have prolonged the wait for victims' families to receive justice. Mohammed and his alleged co-conspirators — Walid bin Attash, Mustafa al-Hawsawi, and Ammar al-Baluchi — are scheduled to go on trial in June 2028.
Prosecutors initially planned to use a confession obtained from Mohammed at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, where he has been held for nearly two decades.
9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

Firefighter walks through the rubble of the World Trade Center after it was struck by a commercial airliner in a terrorist attack. A hijacked American Airlines Boeing 767, originating from Boston's Logan Airport, struck 1 World Trade Center (north tower) at 8:45 a.m. At 9:03 a.m., a United Airlines 767, also hijacked in Boston, crashed into 2 World Trade Center (south tower).The second tower came down 39 minutes after the first. (Todd Maisel/NY Daily News via Getty Images)
Lt. Col. Michael Schrama set the trial date last month before suppressing the confession. He cited "severe coercion" and noted that Mohammed did not have an opportunity to consult with an attorney.
Mohammed and two of his co-defendants had agreed to a plea deal with the Biden administration in 2024 that would have spared them the death penalty.

The deal was subsequently revoked following public outcry, resulting in further lengthy litigation.
Meanwhile, 9/11 families have asked the Trump administration to declassify documents on Saudi Arabia's alleged role in the attacks.

title: NTSB reveals if crew survived Amazon cargo jet disaster as it shares details about victims
summary: The NTSB said the crew survived after the Amazon cargo plane overran the runway, caught fire and collided with two vehicles carrying eight occupants.
story: NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said the Boeing 767 continued about 1,300 feet beyond the paved runway surface.
Federal regulators said the two crew members aboard the Amazon cargo jet that crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday survived the accident.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) provided the update during a Sunday press conference after officials said the cargo plane overran the runway and caught fire while landing. The crash killed five people and injured five others, authorities said Sunday.
The jet collided with two vehicles carrying at least eight occupants, according to NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy.

Seven of the victims were in a van that was struck and "torn apart" on airport grounds, Homendy said. The 2012 white Ford Econoline van was owned by Ocean Service Corporation, a contract cleaning company that provides services for airlines, she said.
AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED
NTSB investigators examine a wreckage field Monday after a Boeing 767 cargo plane overran the end of Runway 30 while landing Sunday at Miami International Airport. (@NTSB_Newsroom/X)
The NTSB said the aircraft then crashed through the airport perimeter and struck a civilian vehicle, a Toyota Corolla Cross LE, that was traveling on Northwest 67th Avenue.
Homendy said investigators observed what appeared to be deployed airbags in the vehicles as they surveyed the crash site.
"You can see components from vehicles, both passenger vehicles and the aircraft itself," Homendy said.
The jet then "continued into the grass and impacted another fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed," Homendy said.

An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 crashes off the runway and crushes a vehicle near the Miami International Airport in Miami on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026.  (Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
In total, the jet reportedly traveled 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface.
Homendy said the wreckage was "extensive," noting that the crash damaged airport navigational aids and equipment, while fencing was ripped apart throughout the area.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Officials investigate a Prime Air cargo plane at Miami International Airport after it overran the runway at Miami International Airport in Miami, Florida, on September 6, 2026. (CHANDAN KHANNA / AFP via Getty Images)
Officials said the Boeing 767 had completed two other flights before crashing in Miami, where its operator, 21 Air LLC, is based.
The aircraft traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, then from Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico, before returning to Miami, Homendy said.
NTSB investigators have recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder, which they planned to examine.
Prime Air flight 7598 became disabled after overrunning Miami International Airport’s diagonal runway. (Google Maps)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Homendy described the crash site as "devastating," saying wreckage was scattered throughout the area.
"I would describe it in one word, devastating, utter devastation," she said.
"I mean, you can see on the paved surface, tire marks that continue through the grass. There's debris everywhere."
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Menendez brothers granted 2027 parole hearing a year earlier than expected
summary: Erik and Lyle Menendez will face a parole hearing in March 2027, moved up from 2028 reportedly under Proposition 9 provisions after their resentencing.
story: Former Sacramento DA Anne Marie Schubert is spearheading a lawsuit challenging new California Board of Parole Hearings guidelines that she warns will open a pathway to freedom for serial killers, mass shooters and more of the state's worst violent criminals.
Erik and Lyle Menendez have been granted a parole hearing for next year, a year earlier than previously expected.

The brothers, who were both convicted of the Aug. 20, 1989, shotgun slayings of their parents, Jose and Mary Louise "Kitty" Menendez, in their Beverly Hills home, are scheduled to have a parole suitability hearing in March 2027 instead of August 2028, Fox News confirms.

The change stems from two provisions included in Proposition 9, which allow a prison inmate's next parole hearing date to be moved up if there is a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole, The Orange County Register reported.
CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM
Erik and Lyle Menendez will face a parole board hearing in March 2027, a year earlier than expected. (Getty Images)

"For almost 40 years, Erik and Lyle have worked to take responsibility for their actions, confront and heal from the unimaginable abuse and trauma they endured, grow as individuals, and dedicate themselves to serving others," a statement by family members reads.

"Through efforts such as helping to establish a hospice program and creating Green Space, they have sought to build an environment that reminds people serving life sentences that their lives still have meaning and that, regardless of their circumstances, they can choose each day to grow, heal, accept accountability, and contribute something of value to the world around them," they added.
NEW HAMPSHIRE RESENTENCING GIVES DARTMOUTH KILLER ROBERT TULLOCH A PAROLE PATH AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

Lyle, left, and Erik Menendez leave a courtroom in Santa Monica, Calif., Aug. 6, 1990, after a judge ruled that conversations between the brothers and their psychologist after their parents were slain were not privileged and could be used as evidence. (AP Photo/Nick Ut, File)

The brothers were handed life sentences without the possibility of parole for the murders, which drew widespread media attention. However, they were resentenced to life in May 2025, making them eligible for parole.
The new sentencing came amid a push by supporters following a Netflix series on the case that resurrected calls for their freedom. They were denied parole last year.
NEVADA PAROLE BOARD REJECTS HENRY RUGGS III'S BID FOR EARLY RELEASE AFTER DEADLY 156 MPH DUI CRASH
Erik Menendez appears remotely for a 2025 parole hearing. (CDCR)
The brothers have said the murders were committed after years of sexual abuse by their father. However, prosecutors have contested the claims, arguing the pair killed their parents out of greed.

"Erik and Lyle were once sentenced to life without the possibility of parole," the family statement said. "We will always be profoundly grateful that they have been resentenced and that our family can now imagine a future in which they are once again part of our everyday lives… We are incredibly proud of the men they have become and deeply grateful to the Parole Board for recognizing their efforts and allowing them to advance their parole hearing."
A sketch depicts (l-r) Erik and Lyle Menendez as they appear remotely at superior court in Van Nuys, California, Friday, April 11, 2025. (Bill Robles)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lyle Menendez, 58, and Erik Menendez, 55, are both incarcerated in the Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility in San Diego.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Supporters of Alabama school bus driver charged in deadly accident say she suffered from 'medical crisis'
summary: Theresa McCloud faces vehicular homicide charges after a fatal Auburn school bus crash, but supporters claim a sudden blood sugar drop caused the accident.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
An Alabama woman accused of causing a deadly crash while driving a school bus experienced a medical crisis during the accident, her supporters reportedly said.
Theresa McCloud, 75, faces charges of vehicular homicide and criminal negligence for the Nov. 18, 2025 crash in Auburn.
McCloud was driving a bus for Auburn City Schools when she struck a vehicle. Jennifer Leigh Cooper, 42, a well-known local bakery owner, was killed in the collision, AL.com reported.
HEART-STOPPING VIDEO SHOWS MIDDLE SCHOOLERS SAVING THEIR BUS AFTER DRIVER PASSES OUT AT THE WHEEL
Morning light is "crucial to regulate sleep, [boost] alertness and support mental health," according to a sleep expert. (iStock)

McCloud's supporters said she suffered a medical crisis during the fatal crash. However, a lawsuit filed by Cooper's husband against McCloud and the Auburn City Schools Board of Education alleges that McCloud had diabetes and had been prescribed opiates.

On the day of the accident, McCloud told her supervisors that she was not feeling well, the lawsuit states. Two days prior, she had visited a doctor who prescribed opiates to help with her symptoms. Those medications came with a warning label against driving while taking them, according to the suit.
"Theresa’s blood sugar suddenly dropped to 23 mg/dL while driving, causing confusion and loss of consciousness," stated a GoFundMe page that has since been removed.
OLDER ADULTS TAKING 5 OR MORE PRESCRIPTION DRUGS FACE HIGHER RISK OF DEATH, STUDY FINDS

A school bus takes students home in the small Tulare County town in 2023. Supporters of an Alabama school bus driver charged in the vehicle death of a woman said she suffered a medical crisis during the deadly accident. (Genaro Molina / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"Theresa had never experienced a low blood sugar episode before, and doctors confirmed that this was a medical crisis," the page continued. "Even so, Theresa is now facing the overwhelming challenge of defending against charges connected to that emergency. On September 4, 2026, Theresa turned herself in and began facing the legal process head-on."
While driving, McCloud lost control "based on either her known medical conditions, her use of opiates and/or a mix of both," the lawsuit alleges.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The suit further said that the opiates and her diabetes "severely impaired her ability to drive any vehicle and made her unable to perform her duties as a bus driver," according to the newspaper. McCloud's family reportedly disputes the allegations.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the school district.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Ritzy Miami steakhouse manager held on ICE detainer after mom found stabbed to death
summary: Surveillance video allegedly shows the Miami steakhouse manager blood-soaked in an elevator with a knife hours after returning home with his mother.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Miami steakhouse manager allegedly emerged from his luxury apartment covered in blood and clutching a knife before telling police he had acted in self-defense after his mother was found stabbed to death inside.
Stefano Eduardo Cremasco-Cicero, 36, told officers, "I was defending myself," after Miami police were called to the Brickell high-rise early Friday, according to an arrest report obtained by WPLG.
Cremasco-Cicero is charged with second-degree murder with a weapon, Miami-Dade County jail records show.
KARMELO ANTHONY STAYS SILENT AS ANALYSTS WARN DEFENSE FACES UPHILL BATTLE IN TRACK MEET STABBING TRIAL
Stefano Cremasco-Cicero is being held without bond on a second-degree murder charge and an ICE detainer. (Miami-Dade County Corrections and Rehabilitation)
Officers were dispatched at about 4:47 a.m. for an "unknown request for police assistance," according to the outlet.
Officers found Cremasco-Cicero in the lobby with blood on his hands, clothing and shoes, the outlet reported.
He allegedly directed officers upstairs to the apartment.
Inside the apartment, police found his mother lying behind the front door with multiple apparent stab wounds, according to WPLG. Miami Fire Rescue pronounced her dead shortly after 5 a.m.
FLORIDA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING MOM AND BURNING BODY BECAUSE SHE ‘WANTED TO BE CREMATED’
Cremasco-Cicero was reportedly found in the lobby with blood on his hands, clothing and shoes. (WSVN)
Authorities have not publicly identified the woman or disclosed her age. Police said she was visiting from Mexico and staying with her son.
The unusual chain of events began when a food delivery driver arrived at the building and encountered Cremasco-Cicero in the lobby, according to the report.

He allegedly opened the door for the driver and asked her to call 911. Cremasco-Cicero ultimately placed the call himself but handed the phone to the woman so she could give the dispatcher the building information, WPLG reported.

The driver noticed blood on him as they waited for police, according to the outlet. When she tried to return his phone, he allegedly refused to take it, and she later handed it to responding officers.
THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?
Investigators then turned to surveillance video and building access records to piece together what happened in the hours before police arrived.
Police were called to a high-rise in the Brickell neighborhood of Miami early Friday. (WSVN)
Surveillance video showed Cremasco-Cicero and his mother returning to the building together at about 10:32 p.m. Thursday, according to WPLG. They were reportedly alone in the elevator.
COURTNEY CLENNEY'S DEFENSE INSPECTS KNIVES AT CENTER OF ONLYFANS MODEL'S MURDER CASE AHEAD OF TRIAL: REPORT

At about 4:26 a.m., surveillance video allegedly captured Cremasco-Cicero entering an elevator wearing a white shirt, khaki pants and white shoes that appeared to be covered in blood. Police said he was carrying a knife.
He allegedly dropped the knife after stepping out of the elevator, picked it back up and rode another elevator upstairs, according to the report.

Investigators said Cremasco-Cicero later reappeared in a different, long-sleeved blue shirt and walked out of the building while using his phone. He returned minutes later and sat on a couch in the lobby before flagging down the delivery driver, WPLG reported.
Cremasco-Cicero’s wife, who was in France at the time, told detectives that his mother had been staying with him at the time of the incident, according to local reports. (WSVN)
Police said Cremasco-Cicero had small cuts on his hands and blood residue on his body and clothing. Crime scene investigators photographed him and collected his clothes, according to the outlet.
5 REASONS MORE AMERICANS ARE CUTTING OFF THEIR OWN PARENTS, ACCORDING TO PSYCHOLOGIST

After obtaining a search warrant, homicide detectives allegedly recovered several kitchen knives with blood on them, blood-spattered shirts, broken glass and a broken wine bottle from the apartment, WPLG reported.

Cremasco-Cicero’s wife told detectives she was in France attending a wedding when the killing happened, according to the report. She said her husband and his mother had not been close since his parents divorced and that he had recently been under stress while preparing to open a restaurant in Coconut Grove.
Stefano Cremasco-Cicero is seen sitting for an interview with WSVN-TV about his restaurant in July. (WSVN)
The Miami Herald identified Cremasco-Cicero as the U.S. operating manager of the high-end 1986 Steakhouse in Miami.
The arrest report identified Cremasco-Cicero as a Miami resident through an investor visa, according to WPLG.

Miami-Dade Corrections records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Cremasco-Cicero was booked Friday night and is being held at the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center. The records list no bond, a domestic-violence designation and a hold for immigration authorities.
The jail record does not provide additional details about the immigration hold.
A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital that Cremasco-Cicero is an illegal immigrant.

"On August 5, 2026, ICE lodged a detainer for Stefano Eduardo Cremasco Cicero, a criminal illegal alien from Mexico, charged with homicide," the DHS spokesperson said. "We are calling on Florida to honor our detainer. His claims will be heard by an immigration judge and he will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law."
"Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, if you break the law, you will face the consequences," the spokesperson added. "Criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the U.S."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A motive for the killing remains unclear.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Miami Police Department, the Miami-Dade Clerk of Courts and 1986 Steakhouse for additional information.

title: Two men die within 24 hours at Burning Man as tens of thousands gather in the Nevada desert
summary: Craigh Mann, 60, was found dead by campmates at Burning Man on Saturday, just one day after another participant suffered a fatal medical emergency.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Two men died within roughly 24 hours at Burning Man as tens of thousands of "burners" gathered in the Nevada desert for the final days of the famed festival.

One of the men, identified as 60-year-old Craigh Mann, was found dead by campmates Saturday afternoon, festival organizers said. Another participant in his mid-50s died after suffering a medical emergency a day earlier.
Mann was found at his camp in Black Rock City at about 3 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 5, according to the Burning Man Project.
BURNING MAN MURDER MYSTERY DEEPENS AS NEW DETAILS EMERGE 1 YEAR AFTER DESERT FESTIVAL KILLING

"Burning Man Project is saddened to share that a second Black Rock City participant, Craigh Mann, a 60-year-old man, was found deceased by campmates in his camp," organizers said in a statement.

BURNING MAN HOMICIDE UNSOLVED AS WITNESS REPORTEDLY RECALLS CHILLING ENCOUNTER
He was pronounced dead at the center. Organizers did not provide further details about the type of medical emergency.

"The safety and well-being of our community and staff remain our highest priority," organizers said after the first death. They said support resources were available around the clock for people in Black Rock City, the temporary city built each year to host the event.

A Vantor satellite image shows the center of the Burning Man festival site in Black Rock City, Nev., on Aug. 31, 2026, with its distinctive circular layout and numerous temporary structures. (DigitalGlobe/Getty Images)

title: Alleged cryptoscam ringleader set for plea hearing in $240M bitcoin theft
summary: Malone Lam allegedly used a social engineering attack to steal over 4,100 Bitcoin, then blew millions on Lamborghinis, nightclubs and mansions.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A 22-year-old Singapore man accused of helping steal more than $240 million in Bitcoin from a single victim and splurging the proceeds on luxury cars, private jets, mansions and wild nights out is expected to plead guilty this week in one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts in U.S. history.

Malone Lam, an eighth-grade dropout from Singapore whom prosecutors have identified as a suspected ringleader of the sprawling cryptocurrency scheme, is scheduled for a plea agreement hearing Tuesday in federal court in Washington, D.C.

Lam and his alleged co-conspirators were part of an alleged network of young men in their late teens and early 20s who prosecutors say used a sophisticated "social engineering" attack in August 2024 to trick a wealthy, longtime cryptocurrency investor into handing over access to his digital holdings.
GLOBAL TASK FORCE DISMANTLES 'PIG-BUTCHERING' CRYPTO FRAUD RINGS PREYING ON AMERICANS
This Justice Department court filing in the case against Hamza Doost and Kunal Mehta, which includes a photo of Malone Lam, is photographed Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Jon Elswick)

According to prosecutors, members of the group contacted the victim while posing as representatives of Google and the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange, warning him that his accounts had been compromised.

The scammers allegedly convinced the victim to give them access to his Google Drive and provide security codes that allowed Lam and others to siphon off more than 4,100 Bitcoin, then worth over $240 million.
The group allegedly moved the stolen cryptocurrency through multiple exchange platforms and used money laundering specialists to convert portions of it into cash.
Prosecutors say Lam and his associates then embarked on a staggering spending spree.
This Justice Department's grand jury superseding indictment against Malone Lam and his co-defendants is photographed Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Jon Elswick)

Lam and his friends allegedly spent $4 million at Los Angeles nightclubs in roughly a month, including more than $569,000 that Lam allegedly spent during a single night out. He also allegedly used stolen cryptocurrency to purchase a $2 million watch and more than 30 vehicles, including custom Porsches, Lamborghinis and Ferraris.
The group also rented multimillion-dollar homes, flew on private jets and hired private security.
The alleged spending was so lavish that the judge overseeing Lam's initial court appearance in Miami invoked a famous Hollywood troublemaker after hearing a prosecutor describe it.
"I could only think of Ferris Bueller gone bad," U.S. Magistrate Judge Alicia Valle said, referring to the school-skipping protagonist of the 1986 movie "Ferris Bueller's Day Off."
FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS
The lavish lifestyle quickly attracted attention as investigators closed in.

One alleged co-conspirator, Jeandiel Serrano, failed to conceal his IP address while creating an account on a cryptocurrency exchange that held nearly $30 million in stolen funds, prosecutors said. Investigators traced the address to an Encino, California, home Serrano was renting for $47,500 per month.
This Justice Department court filing in the case against Hamza Doost and Kunal Mehta, which includes a photo of Malone Lam, is photographed Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Jon Elswick)

Serrano and Lam were arrested separately on Sept. 18, 2024. FBI agents took Serrano into custody at Los Angeles International Airport, where authorities said he was wearing a watch worth roughly $500,000.
Lam was arrested the same day at a Miami mansion.
Eighteen defendants have been charged in connection with the case, with ten already pleading guilty.

At Lam's initial court appearance, a prosecutor estimated that federal sentencing guidelines could call for a prison term of at least 14 years if he is convicted.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Florida AG seeks death penalty for couple who allegedly held 4 children in ‘rolling prison’ for over 6 years
summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier says his office will seek the death penalty for two adults who allegedly confined four children to a truck cab.
story: Keisha Epps, 51, and Tamra Stewart, 37, face child sexual battery, molestation and neglect charges after investigators say they kept four children inside the cab of a tractor-trailer for more than six years. (FOX 35)

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier says his office will seek the death penalty for the two adults who allegedly confined four children to the cab of a tractor-trailer, some for more than six years, and sexually abused them.

Keisha Monique Epps, 51, and Tamra Marshon Stewart, 37, have been charged with sexual battery, molestation and neglect of two girls and two boys — two 5-year-olds, a 6-year-old and a 9-year-old, Uthmeier said.

Epps and Stewart, who has been identified as her fiancé, had been living in the cab with the children. Epps worked as a truck driver, frequenting a route between Miami and Atlanta, according to court documents.
FLORIDA COUPLE ALLEGEDLY HELD FOUR CHILDREN IN TRACTOR-TRAILER CAB FOR NEARLY SEVEN YEARS
Keisha Epps and Tamra Marshon Stewart were arrested Aug. 6 and remain jailed as they await trial on child neglect charges. (Jacksonville Sheriff's Office)
"These children were trapped in a rolling prison and abused by the adults who were supposed to protect them," Uthmeier said.
"We will pursue with everything we have the death penalty. We will seek executions, if you want to come in here [in Florida] and you want to physically molest, abuse, and violate our little kids."
Florida law allows prosecutors to seek the death penalty for adults convicted of sexual battery against a child younger than 12.
The two girls were sexually abused by Stewart for years, Uthmeier said. When the two boys witnessed sexual abuse and confronted Stewart, he "beat them by punching them in their heads," reports show.

The children told authorities that they had told Epps about the sexual abuse and saw her witness it. She called one of the children "derogatory names" and continued to leave them alone with Stewart, reports show.
Stewart told investigators he had committed three sexual batteries against one of the girls, according to Uthmeier’s office.
One of the children was found to have an untreated sexually transmitted infection, Uthmeier’s office said.
But the horrors allegedly went far beyond sexual abuse.
The couple confined the children in the truck cab without "time to take showers, use the restroom" or "exercise outside," investigators wrote in their reports.
FLORIDA-LED OPERATION RESCUES 163 CHILDREN AROUND GLOBE IN HISTORIC STATE SWEEP, HUNTS SUSPECTED PREDATORS
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier speaks at a news conference in Kissimmee, Fla., on Sept. 1, 2026. (Florida Office of the Attorney General)
"This case is one of, if not the most, horrific that my team has ever had to work on," Uthmeier said at a news conference in Kissimmee, Florida, on Sept. 1.

Over the years of their imprisonment, the children were forced to "use the bathroom" in cups and paper bags, he said. When making stops, "the adults would go to the restroom," Uthmeier said. "They might take a shower, but they would leave the kids locked in this rolling dungeon."
"As a result of the abuse" over the years, he said, the children "suffer severe physical infirmities."
The children were kept inside the vehicle "for the majority of their days," court records show.

The children said they hadn’t been "allowed to attend school for approximately five years," according to an arrest report. A detective on the case reported the children were "walking with an unnatural gait from being confined to the cab."

title: Former USCIS official, accomplice charged in alleged $960K citizenship bribery scheme
summary: A former USCIS official and his accomplice allegedly accepted nearly $960,000 in bribes to fast-track citizenship applications, skipping key checks.
story: Host Kayleigh McEnany reveals how immigration fraud is under fire as authorities target multiple illegal operations. The Department of Justice charged 11 people with organizing over 1,000 sham marriages to abuse the visa system. Meanwhile, Texas officials are cracking down on birth tourism centers offering instant American citizenship to newborns of Chinese nationals.

A former senior U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services official and his accomplice are facing charges for an alleged bribery scheme in which they accepted nearly $960,000 in exchange for favors in the processing of immigration benefit applications, including citizenship cases.

The former official, Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu, and his financial accomplice, Adeniyi Akeem Somoye, were arrested on federal charges for their roles in an alleged multi‑year scheme to receive illegal gratuities in exchange for manipulating and expediting immigration applications, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas.
The pair were charged with conspiracy to receive illegal gratuities by a public official, and they were arrested on Wednesday.
Investigators found extensive WhatsApp messages between Ganiyu, Somoye and numerous applicants whose immigration cases they handled, including thousands of messages and hundreds of calls.
FEDS BUST ONE OF LARGEST ALLEGED MARRIAGE FRAUD SCHEMES IN US HISTORY INVOLVING 1,000-PLUS CHINESE SHAM UNIONS

A former senior USCIS official and his accomplice are facing charges for an alleged bribery scheme in which they accepted nearly $960,000 in exchange for favors in the citizenship application process. (John Moore/Getty Images)

Between December 2019 and March 2026, the duo allegedly bypassed standard procedures by pushing applicants who paid bribes directly to Ganiyu, skipping key steps in the immigration process such as criminal background checks, interviews, standard USCIS processing protocols and other reviews, according to prosecutors.
Prosecutors allege Ganiyu altered the USCIS system to fast-track applications in exchange for money.
He allegedly fast-tracked citizenship for Somoye before he approved residency applications for Somoye’s wife and child.
Ganiyu allegedly rerouted applications from USCIS field offices in Minneapolis, Charlotte and Houston, bypassing local supervisors so he could approve them himself.
FEDS SEIZE $40M IN GOLD BARS, CASH, ROLEXES FROM FORMER CIA OFFICIAL WHO FAKED BEING A NAVY PILOT
The pair were charged with conspiracy to receive illegal gratuities by a public official. (Robert Nickelsberg/Getty Images)

Ganiyu received about $671,438 from citizenship applicants through Zelle and Cash App, along with $287,830 in cash deposits that prosecutors say were meant to conceal the money’s source, according to court documents, the New York Post reported.

Acting as the alleged financial intermediary, Somoye processed roughly $1.7 million in transfers involving applicants, including through bank accounts, Zelle and Cash App, allegedly keeping a portion of the payments. He also deposited $449,010 in cash, court documents show, according to the New York Post.
The complaint alleges that Ganiyu and Somoye often exchanged money "back and forth" with applicants.
Most of the citizenship applications they handled involved applicants from African countries, according to prosecutors.
Each defendant faces up to five years in federal prison and a fine of up to $250,000. (Robert Nickelsberg / Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
According to prosecutors, Ganiyu resigned from USCIS in March, citing "personal reasons," several months before his arrest.

"Selling immigration benefits for cash is a blatant abuse of public trust," U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould said in a statement. "When a federal official puts a price tag on lawful status, we will intervene immediately."
Each defendant faces up to five years in federal prison and a fine of up to $250,000.

title: Stray bullet from nearby lounge fight kills Frito-Lay worker inside Sam's Club
summary: Nashville police say a Frito-Lay worker was killed by a stray bullet inside Sam's Club after an argument spilled outside Lavo Lounge on Antioch Pike.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A deadly argument outside a Nashville lounge sent a bullet tearing through the metal wall of a nearby Sam’s Club, killing an innocent Frito-Lay worker as he counted products in the chip aisle, police said.

The victim, identified as 55-year-old Paris Carlock of Murfreesboro, was conducting an early-morning product inventory near the middle of the store shortly after 4 a.m. when the bullet struck him in the head.
Sam’s Club staff rushed to Carlock’s aid before he was transported to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead, according to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department.
POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN AFTER WALMART EMPLOYEE SHOT DURING DISPUTE IN PENNSYLVANIA

A Metro Nashville Police vehicle sits outside the Sam’s Club where Frito-Lay employee Paris Carlock was fatally struck by a bullet that pierced the store’s wall. (Metropolitan Nashville Police Department)
Investigators believe the gunfire was connected to an argument that began inside Lavo Lounge on Antioch Pike, just down the street from the Sam’s Club.
Police said security removed the people involved from the lounge, but the dispute reportedly spilled outside and continued. Gunshots were heard as multiple vehicles left the area.
MISSOURI MOM OF 5 FATALLY SHOT WHILE BUYING SLUSHIES WITH CHILDREN; POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN
A bullet from gunfire on Antioch Pike pierced the metal side wall of a Sam’s Club and struck Paris Carlock as he conducted inventory inside, police said. (Metropolitan Nashville Police Department)
One of those bullets pierced the Sam’s Club’s exterior wall and struck Carlock as he worked inside, police said.
The department described Carlock as an "innocent" victim.
POLICE SWARM MICHIGAN SHOPPING CENTER AFTER 'SIGNIFICANT' SHOOTING INCIDENT; AT LEAST 2 DEAD
Police said an argument began inside Lavo Lounge before spilling outside and ending in gunfire that killed an innocent Frito-Lay worker inside a nearby Sam’s Club. (Google Maps)
Homicide Unit detectives are pursuing leads, but police have not announced any arrests or released descriptions of the people or vehicles involved.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of one of our colleagues," a PepsiCo spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "Our sincere condolences are with their family members and loved ones. We have been working closely with law enforcement and local officials regarding the matter."

title: Amazon cargo plane overruns Miami airport runway and strikes 'multiple' vehicles; 5 dead, 5 injured
summary: All runways and taxiways at Miami International Airport were closed after an Amazon cargo jet, a Boeing 767-300, overran the runway, officials said.
story: Fox News correspondent Madison Scarpino reports on the emergency response underway at Miami International Airport after an Amazon cargo jet overran the runway, struck multiple vehicles and caught fire on ‘Fox Report.’

At least five people were killed, and five others were injured at Miami International Airport on Sunday after an Amazon cargo plane overran the runway, struck multiple vehicles and caught fire while landing.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office (MDSO) and Miami-Dade Fire Rescue (MDFR) confirmed that there were at least 10 victims involved in the crash, which happened when Prime Air flight 7598 overran Miami International Airport’s diagonal runway at about 2 p.m. local time.
An Amazon spokesperson expressed condolences to those impacted.

"We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport. Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss," the company said.
Emergency personnel respond to Miami International Airport following an Amazon cargo plane crash on Sept. 6, 2026, in Miami. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT
Fire Chief Raied Jadallah said three people were taken to a trauma center in critical condition and two others were transported to a local hospital.
Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said the rescue team "was there within seconds of the crash."
Fire officials are still working to contain a fuel leak caused by the crash, according to Jadallah.
"We do still have an active fuel leak that's occurring off of the aircraft that is being mitigated," Jadallah said.
Fire officials told Fox News Digital that the fire erupted from the aircraft’s engine, but HazMat units were able to safely shut down the engine while addressing the plane’s fuel leak.
"Firefighters encountered a complex engine compartment fire and used foam from specialized airport firefighting units to extinguish the flames," officials said.

An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 crashes off the runway and crushes a vehicle west of Miami International Airport in Miami on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026.  (Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
MDFR said several victims were trapped in the vehicles struck by the airplane, with one requiring "extrication" by specialized technical rescue personnel.

Crews also conducted search-and-rescue operations for the pilots and co-pilots, who officials said were trapped inside the cockpit. They also worked to locate and assess patients throughout the scene.
More than 60 fire units and about 200 personnel responded to the scene after the airplane crashed and came to a stop beyond the airport operations boundary, according to fire officials.
Prime Air flight 7598 became disabled after overrunning Miami International Airport’s diagonal runway. (Google Maps)

"Units arrived to find an airplane that had caught on fire as a result of this crash, with heavy flames and smoke showing. Firefighters are working on extinguishing the fire and assessing patients," the Miami-Dade Fire Rescue said in a post on X.
MDFR is now operating in a supportive role, with units remaining on scene to assist partner agencies.
An Amazon spokesperson said the plane experienced an "incident" while attempting to land, but did not elaborate on the circumstances.
"We can confirm that an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air experienced an incident while attempting to land at Miami International Airport today," Amazon said.

"This is a fast-moving situation and we're still gathering details. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened. Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved. We're doing everything we can to support those affected."
Boeing told Fox News that the aircraft was first delivered as a passenger plane in 1994 before later being converted to a freighter.

"Boeing extends our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the accident in Miami. Our hearts go out to those injured and affected by this tragedy. Boeing is supporting the investigation led by the U.S National Transportation Safety Board," the aerospace manufacturer said.

Officials investigate a Prime Air cargo plane at Miami International Airport after it overran the runway at Miami International Airport in Miami, Florida, on September 6, 2026. (CHANDAN KHANNA / AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300, departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
County CAD records indicate the emergency call was received at about 1:55 p.m.
Cava said the city is closely monitoring the situation.
"Right now, our focus is on everyone involved and making sure our first responders have what they need. We will provide updates as we learn more," she said in a post on X.
A Prime Air cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport Sunday afternoon.  (WSNV)
Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said first responders were assessing the scene.

"We’ve issued a full ground stop at Miami International while first responders assess the scene after an Amazon cargo plane overran the runway. If you’re traveling through the area, please expect significant delays and potential cancellations," he said in a post on X.
Airport officials later said one runway reopened, but they are "still experiencing impacts from this incident."
Passengers with flights scheduled for Sunday were advised to check directly with their airline for flight status updates before heading to the airport.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The FAA will investigate the incident.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Hikers stranded on Mount Shasta after relying on AI to plan trip, sheriff says
summary: Three Roseville hikers used Google's Gemini AI to plan a Mount Shasta climb but ended up stranded overnight in a steep canyon, authorities said.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A trio of novice hikers who turned to AI to help plan their climb up California’s Mount Shasta ended up stranded overnight in a steep canyon after their trek went dangerously off course, authorities said.

The three young men from Roseville told a Siskiyou County sheriff’s deputy after their rescue that they had relied heavily on Google Gemini for information about the route and what to pack for the trip.

That proved to be a "critical misstep," the sheriff’s office said, because Gemini advised them to bring far less food and water than they needed when their planned eight-hour ascent stretched into a multi-day ordeal.
CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER

The sheriff's office said serious accidents and deaths have occurred when people became lost and wandered into more dangerous areas such as the Mud Creek drainage. (Facebook/Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office)
The hikers made camp at about 8,400 feet on Saturday, Aug. 29, then set out with daypacks for the summit at 3 a.m. Sunday.
They did not reach the top until 7 p.m. — seven hours after the recommended noon turnaround time — leaving them to descend in the dark.
About an hour later, the hikers called the sheriff’s office for directions but eventually wandered off the Clear Creek Route and into Mud Creek Canyon.
One of the men later fell and injured his knee, stranding the group in the steep canyon overnight.
A view of Mount Shasta in California as rescuers made their way up to the stranded hikers. (Facebook/Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office)

U.S. Forest Service climbing rangers reached the hikers the next morning and treated the injured man. Siskiyou County Search and Rescue volunteers also were sent to help, and everyone made it back to the trailhead safely.
MISSOURI DEPUTY AG, MISSING 6 DAYS AFTER SEEKING TO SUMMIT WYOMING'S TALLEST PEAK, IS FOUND ALIVE

"It is always advisable to call the local USFS Mount Shasta Ranger Station ahead of your trip to ensure you have the most accurate information, and to never rely solely on AI for your trip planning," the sheriff’s office said.
Climbers who have not reached the summit by noon should turn back, the sheriff’s office said, giving themselves — and rescuers, if needed — enough daylight to get off the mountain.
Rescuers reached the stranded hikers the following morning. All rescuers and the trio of hikers made it safely to the trailhead. (Facebook/Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office)
Hikers should also carry more than one way to navigate and regularly check that they are still on the correct route rather than depending on a cellphone or GPS device.

The Clear Creek Route does not require technical mountaineering, but hikers still need to be fit and prepared for injuries, bad weather or an unexpected night on the mountain, the sheriff’s office said.

title: Missouri foster mom accused of trading teen for monkey avoids prison
summary: Brenda Deutsch received a suspended sentence after allegedly trading a foster teen for a monkey, as the judge called her actions reprehensible.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Missouri foster mother accused of trading a teenage girl for a monkey avoided prison time, even as a judge condemned her as reprehensible and apologized to her alleged victims for a foster care system he said had failed them.

Brenda Deutsch, 70, was sentenced to seven years in prison for child endangerment, but a Lincoln County judge suspended execution of the sentence and placed her on three years of probation, allowing her to remain free if she complies with its terms, FOX2 St. Louis reported.
Judge Thomas Frawley also revoked Deutsch’s foster care license from the bench and criticized the state of Missouri for allowing her to keep it.
FLORIDA COUPLE ALLEGEDLY HELD FOUR CHILDREN IN TRACTOR-TRAILER CAB FOR NEARLY SIX YEARS
Brenda Deutsch is charged with three felony counts of child abuse, neglect and child endangerment. (Lincoln County Sheriff's Office)
Frawley then apologized to the victims in the courtroom, telling them he was sorry the system had failed them.
Deutsch’s biological daughter, Brina Johnson, who testified about alleged abuse, said the outcome was not what she had hoped for.
"I’m kinda lost for words because this is not the end we wished for," Johnson told FOX2.
Johnson said a teenager present in the courtroom was the foster child at the center of allegations that Deutsch traded her for a monkey.
"I have the whole conversation on my phone, which I turned over to the detectives," Johnson said.
"That’s what she did; she had at least seven monkeys," Johnson said. "That’s just her thing. But she wasn’t any nicer to those monkeys than she was to a child."
A judge condemned Brenda Deutsch, 70, as "reprehensible" and said the foster care system had failed her victims. (iStock)
Deutsch was arrested in April after authorities investigated allegations that she sent the foster child, who is now 17, to Texas to stay in a home Deutsch admitted in court she knew nothing about.

Court documents previously obtained by Fox News Digital said the investigation began after Deutsch sought permission to take the girl to visit a friend in Texas. Five days later, an anonymous caller alerted the Missouri Department of Social Services Children’s Division that Deutsch was allegedly physically and mentally abusing the child.
Investigators later learned of an allegation that the girl had been traded for an exotic animal and was living in Texas.
69 LIVE ANIMALS FOUND STUFFED IN PILLOWCASES IN HIDDEN CAR COMPARTMENT AFTER BORDER ARREST: FEDS
The teenager told investigators Deutsch informed her Texas friend that the friend could keep the child, but Deutsch "will be keeping the check," according to court documents.
A witness told police the girl had been left in an unsanitary Texas home filled with exotic animals. She was eventually taken into the custody of child protective services in Texas.

Deutsch was arrested in April after authorities investigated allegations that she sent the foster child, who is now 17, to Texas to stay in a home Deutsch admitted in court she knew nothing about. (iStock)

The teenager also described alleged abuse by Deutsch, telling investigators she was struck with objects including a paddle and shoes. During one alleged beating, she said she lay on the floor and tried to "soften the strikes to her body," according to court documents.
Deutsch also allegedly took away the girl’s clothes and once threatened to kill her "if she did not shut up," the documents said.
Deutsch declined to comment outside the courthouse, shielding her face with a piece of paper as she walked to her vehicle and drove away.
Deutsch has reportedly fostered more than 200 children over the years.
Johnson said the judge’s acknowledgment of the system’s failures offered some validation despite her disappointment with the outcome.

title: Texas deputy screams and runs after 'dead' deer springs to feet in viral encounter
summary: The viral video has racked up over 10 million views as an East Texas sheriff's deputy discovers a motionless doe is very much alive during a night shift, a sheriff said.
story: A Texas deputy got the scare of a lifetime when a "dead" deer suddenly jumped up to its feet on the side of a roadway, a sheriff said. (Credit: Sheriff Woody Wallace via Storyful)

An East Texas sheriff’s deputy got the scare of his life when a deer he thought was dead suddenly sprang to its feet, sending the startled lawman screaming back toward his cruiser in a moment caught on camera that quickly went viral online.
The wild encounter was captured on the deputy’s dashcam and shared on Facebook by Trinity County Sheriff Woody Wallace, who joked that sometimes things can "scare the heck out of a person."
Wallace had some fun with the incident, encouraging social media users to "[w]atch when he encounters what he thinks is a dead deer until it comes back to life!"
The video opens with the deputy approaching what appears to be a motionless doe lying along the side of the road.

Karmelo Anthony’s family is seeking another $250,000 to fund his appeal after an earlier campaign raised nearly $634,000 and faced questions over how the money was spent, the family announced at a news conference in Dallas, Texas.

The fundraising push came nearly two weeks after a judge denied Anthony’s request for a new trial. His family and supporters, including attorney Russell Wilson, used the Dallas news conference to outline the appeal.

Anthony, 19, was sentenced to 35 years in prison in June after a jury convicted him of murdering 17-year-old Austin Metcalf during a high school track meet in Frisco, Texas. He has appealed and says he cannot afford to hire an attorney for the appeal.

Left: Karmelo Anthony is seen in a prison mugshot. Right: Austin Metcalf, who was stabbed to death by Anthony. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice; Jeff Metcalf)

KARMELO ANTHONY BLASTS JUDGE IN NEW FILING OVER HANDLING OF MURDER TRIAL

Wilson said the appeal could take more than a year. The trial record is expected to be assembled in October. After that, both sides will make their case in writing, and the Dallas Court of Appeals could hold a hearing.

Karmelo Anthony's mother, Kayla Hayes, speaks at a press conference in April. (Next Generation Action Network via Facebook)

title: California pizza joint allegedly used as meth distribution hub as illegal immigrant charged
summary: Kawal Preet Singh allegedly used a Round Table Pizza in Dinuba to distribute over 40 pounds of methamphetamine as part of an organized crime network.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A California pizza shop allegedly had far more than pies on the menu, with a man accused of using the Round Table Pizza restaurant to sell massive quantities of meth.

Kawal Preet Singh, a 50-year-old Indian national living illegally in the United States, was indicted Thursday on federal drug and firearm charges after authorities allegedly uncovered more than 40 pounds of methamphetamine, three guns and over $10,000 in cash.

Federal prosecutors say Singh operated the Round Table Pizza restaurant in Dinuba, a Tulare County city about 30 miles southeast of Fresno, and used the business to distribute large quantities of methamphetamine.
CALIFORNIA SUSPECT'S ALLEGED $30K METH STASH SEIZED AFTER HE LEFT BACKPACK IN RIDESHARE: POLICE
Round Table Pizza received 71 price complaints per 1,000 reviews, according to findings shared with Fox News Digital. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)
Singh pleaded not guilty during his arraignment Thursday. He is not in custody, according to The Fresno Bee.
The Dinuba restaurant is listed as permanently closed on Google.
"The employee involved in the reported incident had worked at this location for approximately one and a half months," the company told GV Wire.
Erin Mandzik, senior director of corporate communications for FAT Brands, Round Table Pizza’s parent company, told The Fresno Bee that the restaurant was independently owned and operated.
Mandzik said the local owners had no knowledge of the alleged illegal activity before it came to light and were fully cooperating with authorities, according to the newspaper.
Fox News Digital reached out to Round Table Pizza seeking additional information about Singh’s role, the restaurant’s ownership and the decision to permanently close the location.
FEDS SEIZE MOUNTAIN OF FENTANYL FROM 'OPEN-AIR DRUG MARKET' IN MASSIVE CRACKDOWN TARGETING GANG CREWS
Federal agents allegedly seized more than 40 pounds of methamphetamine while searching Kawal Preet Singh’s home, vehicle and business. (U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California)

Federal agents searched Singh’s home and the restaurant Aug. 18 as part of an investigation into Indian organized crime in California’s Central Valley, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California.
Investigators allegedly found approximately 13.8 kilograms, or more than 30 pounds, of suspected methamphetamine at Singh’s home, The Fresno Bee reported.
CBP OFFICERS SEIZE OVER $2.8M IN COCAINE AND METH IN BACK-TO-BACK BUSTS AT CALIFORNIA PORT OF ENTRY
Federal agents allegedly seized three firearms while searching Kawal Preet Singh’s home and business, prosecutors said. (U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California)
Another roughly 4.9 kilograms, or nearly 11 pounds, was allegedly packed into five clear plastic bags inside Singh’s Hyundai Sonata parked at the restaurant, according to the newspaper.
Agents also seized a semiautomatic handgun and $11,800 in cash, the outlet reported.
NEVADA MAN FUNNELED 140 GUNS TO VIOLENT MEXICAN DRUG CARTELS, INCLUDING POWERFUL 'MILITARY-STYLE' RIFLES: DOJ

Photographs released by the Justice Department showed two handguns allegedly seized during the investigation, including one with a teal-colored frame. Another image showed clear plastic bags containing a crystalline substance authorities identified as methamphetamine.
A federal grand jury charged Singh with distribution of methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.
MEXICAN MAFIA TURNED AMERICAN NEIGHBORHOODS INTO ‘GANGSTA’S PARADISE’ WITH MURDERS, KIDNAPPINGS, DRUGS: FEDS
The Round Table Pizza restaurant in Dinuba, California, is listed as permanently closed on Google. (Google Maps)
The investigation reportedly began with a May tip about a suspected narcotics trafficker operating in Fresno and distributing controlled substances.

Investigators later received information about a trafficker known as "Camy," who was described as a Sikh Indian man involved in long-haul trucking, according to court documents cited by The Fresno Bee.
BORDER AGENTS UNCOVER $20M COCAINE STASH HIDDEN BENEATH TRUCK FLOORBOARDS IN MASSIVE BUST

"The information identified the narcotics trafficker as ‘Camy’ and described him as a Sikh Indian male involved in long-haul trucking," an FBI affidavit said, according to the outlet. "The suspect worked with a network of other Sikh Indian truck drivers to transport narcotics."

Investigators developed evidence indicating that a network of truck drivers transported hundreds of kilograms of cocaine from Mexico into the United States for an unidentified Mexican cartel, The Fresno Bee reported. Singh has not been charged with a cocaine-related crime.
The Central Valley High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Task Force later identified Singh as a subject of the investigation, federal prosecutors said.

Search warrants signed Aug. 13 covered Singh, his home and the Dinuba restaurant, according to The Fresno Bee. Five days later, agents allegedly watched Singh leave the restaurant and drive to his home before searching both properties.
Singh allegedly told investigators he had not sold methamphetamine for approximately two months and claimed he was storing the drugs for a friend, according to the outlet.

Singh faces at least 10 years in federal prison if convicted of the drug charges. The firearm count could add at least five more years behind bars.
Prosecutors emphasized that the charges are allegations and that Singh is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
Singh’s next federal court hearing is scheduled for Nov. 4.
