"Sanctions have never changed Mr. Putin's battlefield actions," he said, "so the West is going to have to figure out exactly what they're going to do to Mr. Putin."
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: New Hampshire primaries test Trump and the left
summary: President Donald Trump’s endorsement will be put to the test once again Tuesday in New Hampshire’s primaries, where liberal Democrats are also looking to cap an ascendant primary season with additional victories.
story: President Donald Trump’s endorsement will be put to the test once again Tuesday in New Hampshire’s primaries, where liberal Democrats are also looking to cap an ascendant primary season with additional victories.
Granite State voters are among the last in the country to choose nominees for November’s elections, and Tuesday’s contests will set the matchup in one of this year’s most competitive Senate races.

Trump is hoping his preferred candidate, former GOP Sen. John Sununu, prevails in the primary. On the Democratic side, Rep. Chris Pappas is looking to fend off a democratic socialist opponent for his party’s Senate nomination.
A divisive Democratic battle is also unfolding in one of the state’s competitive House seats, which Pappas left open, while another House Democrat is facing a primary challenger from the left.
Here’s what to watch Tuesday in New Hampshire, where poll closing times vary by municipality, ranging from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. ET.
Senate matchup
Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s retirement opened up this Senate seat, and Republicans are hoping to make the race competitive in November.

Pappas, who has won in a battleground seat since 2018, is considered the front-runner for his party’s nomination. He already appears to be gearing up for the general election, focusing his campaign on addressing high costs and political corruption and already launching an ad attacking a potential Republican opponent.

But Pappas is facing a challenge from the left from Karishma Manzur, a scientist and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who supports progressive policies like “Medicare for All.” Manzur has sharply criticized Pappas over support and funding for Israel, saying he is “enabling genocide.”

The GOP primary includes multiple candidates, but the race is largely between Sununu and another former senator, Scott Brown, who held a Massachusetts seat for three years, previously ran for the New Hampshire Senate in 2014 and served as Trump’s ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa during the president’s first term.
But the president backed Sununu, who also has support from Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

Sununu represented New Hampshire in the Senate from 2003 through 2008 after serving in the House. He lost his bid for re-election in 2008 to Shaheen, but Republicans believe his well-known family name could give him a boost: Sununu’s brother and father both served as governors.

Trump lost the Granite State by just 3 points in 2024, giving Republicans hope about making this open-seat race competitive two years later. The GOP has not won a Senate race there since 2010, but New Hampshire does have a Republican governor, Kelly Ayotte.
Ayotte is running for a second two-year term as one of two GOP governors up for re-election in a state Trump lost two years ago. Ayotte is not facing any major primary challengers.

The Democratic nominee is all but certain to be former New Hampshire Executive Council member Cinde Warmington, who also faces no major competitors and unsuccessfully sought her party’s gubernatorial nomination in 2024.
House battles
The Democratic Party’s divides are on full display in a primary in Pappas’ now-open seat in the 1st District, which includes Manchester, the state’s biggest city.

A crowded field of candidates is running in both parties’ primaries, and the race could be competitive in the fall. Pappas won re-election by 8 points in 2024, but then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried the district by just 2 points.

Two of the front-runners are viewed as the most establishment Democrats: Marine veteran Maura Sullivan, the former congressional candidate and former Defense Department official, and Stefany Shaheen, a health advocate, former Portsmouth City councilwoman and daughter of the retiring senator. Over the weekend, Army National Guard officer Christian Urrutia, who had been running as a progressive, ended his campaign and backed Shaheen.

Another top contender in the race is progressive Carleigh Beriont, a union organizer. Heath Howard, who was backed by the local Democratic Socialists of America chapter, is still on the ballot but dropped out of the race and endorsed Beriont.

On the Republican side, Trump and other Republican leaders have endorsed auto businessman Anthony DiLorenzo. He is facing competition for the GOP nod from state Rep. Brian Cole and Hollie Noveletsky, a military veteran and CEO of her family iron company.
In the state’s other congressional district, Democratic Rep. Maggie Goodlander is facing a primary challenge from state Rep. Paige Beauchemin, a former nurse who entered politics in 2023.

The challenger is running as an unabashed progressive, calling for halting data center construction, new regulations on the artificial intelligence industry, “Medicare for All,” labeling Israel’s conduct in Gaza a “genocide” and abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Although Beauchemin’s campaign is trying to tap into some of the progressive energy that has helped challengers topple incumbents this year, she has struggled to raise money — bringing in $44,000 to Goodlander’s $4.2 million — and hasn’t drawn any outside support from progressive groups.

Goodlander is a first-term lawmaker who recently gained national prominence as one of the national security-minded Democratic lawmakers who made a video telling the military that members could refuse illegal orders. She also worked in the Biden White House and Justice Department, and is married to former Biden national security adviser Jake Sullivan.  Lily Tang Williams, a former Colorado libertarian who since moved to the state, is expected to win the Republican nomination after she lost to Goodlander in 2024.

title: Chinese hackers are running AI on stolen networks to avoid detection, Google says
summary: One China-linked group targets academic, medical and military AI research, the report says.
story: Hackers working for Chinese intelligence are increasingly targeting American AI research and using AI in their operations, Google said Tuesday.

In its latest quarterly report, Google’s Threat Intelligence Group said that several hacker groups, including both intelligence agencies and cybercrime gangs, have moved from basic AI prompting to using AI agents that automate wide swaths of their intrusion.
The switch means hackers spend drastically less time actively hacking, and in some cases can conduct an entire campaign in less than six hours, the report says.

Google said that one Chinese group in particular, which it has tracked since 2023, has relentlessly focused on academic, medical and military research organizations in North America and has specifically gone after proprietary AI research. Google did not name any of the victims.

While American intelligence agencies also have powerful cyberespionage capabilities, the U.S. has long accused China of hacking its companies for economic advantage, a tactic Western countries generally say is unacceptable.
Liu Chang, spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, broadly denied the claims.
“China opposes hacking activities and fights such activities in accordance with the law. That said, we firmly reject vilification and smears under the pretext of cybersecurity,” he said.

Google said it had observed the hacker group compromising unrelated victims’ cloud networks and installing open-source AI models — a way to query models without leaving a trail via commercial AI products.

John Hultquist, the chief analyst at Google’s Threat Intelligence Group, said that running those models on a hacked third-party system allows hackers to avoid monitoring and bypass guardrails that might stop a more popular commercial chatbot from helping with a hacking campaign.
“They compromise a third party and they put models on that third party. They do that instead of using, say, a commercial option where their activities are observed,” Hultquist told NBC News.

The White House has repeatedly cast the U.S. and China as being in a race to develop the most cutting-edge AI. Both American and Chinese AI companies have announced this year that they have developed AI agents that are adept at hacking and cybersecurity operations.

In the last several months, both OpenAI and Anthropic have reported that their own AI agents have slipped out of evaluation sandboxes to reach third-party organizations — incidents that were disclosed after the fact. Google says it has not seen threat actors wage fully automated hacking campaigns but that instead, hacking groups are continuing to layer on more AI into their operations.

To date, there have been no publicly identified government hacking operations conducted entirely by AI agents. But China’s increasing reliance on agentic AI that it has installed on hacked computer networks means the country’s hackers — like any with sufficient resources and who aren’t legally constrained from such activity — can automate more of their work, Hultquist said.

“There were a couple cases where we could see them essentially trying to build out autonomous capabilities, so they can remove themselves, remove humans from the loop on some of their most important tasks,” Hultquist said.

title: Harry and Meghan ‘surprised’ by king’s letter making clear they’re still nonworking royals
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan are “surprised” by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles that reiterated they will remain nonworking members of the royal family after their return to Britain, a spokesperson for the couple told NBC News on Tuesday.
story: LONDON — Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, were “surprised” by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III that confirmed they remain nonworking members of the royal family after their return to Britain, a spokesperson for the couple told NBC News on Tuesday.
Buckingham Palace released the letter Monday, reiterating that Harry and Meghan remained nonworking royals as they have since they stepped down from royal duties in January 2020.
A palace source said the letter was issued to clarify the unchanged position of the couple for the British government and military amid questions over whether the public should fund their security.
It was put into the public domain because it likely would have leaked anyway and the palace wanted to avoid claims of secrecy around what it contained, the source said.
But a spokesman for Harry and Meghan told NBC News that they  were “surprised” by the letter and were not given an opportunity to contribute to its contents.

The contents of the letter were shared with the couple’s staff a few hours before it was released, according to a spokesperson for the Sussexes. A Buckingham Palace source confirmed to NBC News that the letter had been shared with Harry’s team Monday.

A spokesman for Harry and Meghan told NBC News that a government committee was meeting this week, perhaps as early as Tuesday, to discuss whether to provide security for the couple now that they have moved back to the United Kingdom.
The Home Office, the government department responsible for the protection of public figures, declined to respond directly when asked by NBC News, citing security concerns.
A palace source said Monday that it was up to the security committee to decide whether to allocate security for the prince and his family.
The couple moved from California last month for an “extended” stay with their children Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5.

Their surprise return has reignited media coverage of royal tensions, which exploded into public view with the couple’s allegations of racism and bullying. They moved to Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara, and signed a number of commercial deals.
The move back to Britain has also raised a number of questions over security, after a protracted legal battle between Harry and the British government over the removal of their protection.

The long-running dispute stems from a decision by the Home Office in February 2020 that the couple would no longer automatically receive personal police security while in Britain. Harry argues that the government should provide security for him and his family due to his high-profile position, military service in Afghanistan and threats he has received.
The latest public tension follows Monday’s release of the letter signed by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior officer of the royal household.

It said: “It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family.”

It went on to say that their charitable work was “a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity” and “in short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”

It added: “This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected.”

title: New Hampshire primaries test Trump and the left
summary: President Donald Trump’s endorsement will be put to the test once again Tuesday in New Hampshire’s primaries, where liberal Democrats are also looking to cap an ascendant primary season with additional victories.
story: President Donald Trump’s endorsement will be put to the test once again Tuesday in New Hampshire’s primaries, where liberal Democrats are also looking to cap an ascendant primary season with additional victories.
Granite State voters are among the last in the country to choose nominees for November’s elections, and Tuesday’s contests will set the matchup in one of this year’s most competitive Senate races.

Trump is hoping his preferred candidate, former GOP Sen. John Sununu, prevails in the primary. On the Democratic side, Rep. Chris Pappas is looking to fend off a democratic socialist opponent for his party’s Senate nomination.
A divisive Democratic battle is also unfolding in one of the state’s competitive House seats, which Pappas left open, while another House Democrat is facing a primary challenger from the left.
Here’s what to watch Tuesday in New Hampshire, where poll closing times vary by municipality, ranging from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. ET.
Senate matchup
Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s retirement opened up this Senate seat, and Republicans are hoping to make the race competitive in November.

Pappas, who has won in a battleground seat since 2018, is considered the front-runner for his party’s nomination. He already appears to be gearing up for the general election, focusing his campaign on addressing high costs and political corruption and already launching an ad attacking a potential Republican opponent.

But Pappas is facing a challenge from the left from Karishma Manzur, a scientist and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who supports progressive policies like “Medicare for All.” Manzur has sharply criticized Pappas over support and funding for Israel, saying he is “enabling genocide.”

The GOP primary includes multiple candidates, but the race is largely between Sununu and another former senator, Scott Brown, who held a Massachusetts seat for three years, previously ran for the New Hampshire Senate in 2014 and served as Trump’s ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa during the president’s first term.
But the president backed Sununu, who also has support from Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

Sununu represented New Hampshire in the Senate from 2003 through 2008 after serving in the House. He lost his bid for re-election in 2008 to Shaheen, but Republicans believe his well-known family name could give him a boost: Sununu’s brother and father both served as governors.

Trump lost the Granite State by just 3 points in 2024, giving Republicans hope about making this open-seat race competitive two years later. The GOP has not won a Senate race there since 2010, but New Hampshire does have a Republican governor, Kelly Ayotte.
Ayotte is running for a second two-year term as one of two GOP governors up for re-election in a state Trump lost two years ago. Ayotte is not facing any major primary challengers.

The Democratic nominee is all but certain to be former New Hampshire Executive Council member Cinde Warmington, who also faces no major competitors and unsuccessfully sought her party’s gubernatorial nomination in 2024.
House battles
The Democratic Party’s divides are on full display in a primary in Pappas’ now-open seat in the 1st District, which includes Manchester, the state’s biggest city.

A crowded field of candidates is running in both parties’ primaries, and the race could be competitive in the fall. Pappas won re-election by 8 points in 2024, but then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried the district by just 2 points.

Two of the front-runners are viewed as the most establishment Democrats: Marine veteran Maura Sullivan, the former congressional candidate and former Defense Department official, and Stefany Shaheen, a health advocate, former Portsmouth City councilwoman and daughter of the retiring senator. Over the weekend, Army National Guard officer Christian Urrutia, who had been running as a progressive, ended his campaign and backed Shaheen.

Another top contender in the race is progressive Carleigh Beriont, a union organizer. Heath Howard, who was backed by the local Democratic Socialists of America chapter, is still on the ballot but dropped out of the race and endorsed Beriont.

On the Republican side, Trump and other Republican leaders have endorsed auto businessman Anthony DiLorenzo. He is facing competition for the GOP nod from state Rep. Brian Cole and Hollie Noveletsky, a military veteran and CEO of her family iron company.
In the state’s other congressional district, Democratic Rep. Maggie Goodlander is facing a primary challenge from state Rep. Paige Beauchemin, a former nurse who entered politics in 2023.

The challenger is running as an unabashed progressive, calling for halting data center construction, new regulations on the artificial intelligence industry, “Medicare for All,” labeling Israel’s conduct in Gaza a “genocide” and abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Although Beauchemin’s campaign is trying to tap into some of the progressive energy that has helped challengers topple incumbents this year, she has struggled to raise money — bringing in $44,000 to Goodlander’s $4.2 million — and hasn’t drawn any outside support from progressive groups.

Goodlander is a first-term lawmaker who recently gained national prominence as one of the national security-minded Democratic lawmakers who made a video telling the military that members could refuse illegal orders. She also worked in the Biden White House and Justice Department, and is married to former Biden national security adviser Jake Sullivan.  Lily Tang Williams, a former Colorado libertarian who since moved to the state, is expected to win the Republican nomination after she lost to Goodlander in 2024.

title: We want to hear how Medicaid caregiving cuts are affecting you
summary: This article is part of “Disabled and Denied,” a series examining cuts to Medicaid home care and the fallout for disabled people and their families.
story: This article is part of “Disabled and Denied,” a series examining cuts to Medicaid home care and the fallout for disabled people and their families.
NBC News is looking to speak to people who rely on Medicaid-funded care at home, as well as family members, workers and advocates who support them.

For decades, Medicaid home- and community-based services have helped millions of disabled and older Americans live independently rather than in institutions or nursing facilities. Now, a series of changes at the state and federal levels is threatening that system.

President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” is projected to reduce federal Medicaid spending by nearly $1 trillion over the next decade. Conservative officials and activists have increasingly portrayed home care as wasteful and rife with fraud. And the Justice Department has backed away from the federal government’s long-standing interpretation of a landmark Supreme Court ruling protecting the right of disabled people to receive services in their communities.
The Trump administration denies that it’s targeting disability programs, arguing that its efforts to root out waste and abuse will protect Medicaid for vulnerable Americans who need it.
The biggest federal cuts won’t begin to hit until next year, but the system is already showing signs of strain.

In some states, officials have cut wages or capped hours for paid family caregivers. Fraud crackdowns have jeopardized care for families who say they did nothing wrong. And some disabled people have had their caregiving slashed by new algorithmic assessments.

For families who depend on these programs, the stakes are profound. Many fear the changes will unravel a fragile system built over generations to help disabled and older Americans live outside of institutions.

title: Chinese hackers are running AI on stolen networks to avoid detection, Google says
summary: One China-linked group targets academic, medical and military AI research, the report says.
story: Hackers working for Chinese intelligence are increasingly targeting American AI research and using AI in their operations, Google said Tuesday.

In its latest quarterly report, Google’s Threat Intelligence Group said that several hacker groups, including both intelligence agencies and cybercrime gangs, have moved from basic AI prompting to using AI agents that automate wide swaths of their intrusion.
The switch means hackers spend drastically less time actively hacking, and in some cases can conduct an entire campaign in less than six hours, the report says.

Google said that one Chinese group in particular, which it has tracked since 2023, has relentlessly focused on academic, medical and military research organizations in North America and has specifically gone after proprietary AI research. Google did not name any of the victims.

While American intelligence agencies also have powerful cyberespionage capabilities, the U.S. has long accused China of hacking its companies for economic advantage, a tactic Western countries generally say is unacceptable.
Liu Chang, spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, broadly denied the claims.
“China opposes hacking activities and fights such activities in accordance with the law. That said, we firmly reject vilification and smears under the pretext of cybersecurity,” he said.

Google said it had observed the hacker group compromising unrelated victims’ cloud networks and installing open-source AI models — a way to query models without leaving a trail via commercial AI products.

John Hultquist, the chief analyst at Google’s Threat Intelligence Group, said that running those models on a hacked third-party system allows hackers to avoid monitoring and bypass guardrails that might stop a more popular commercial chatbot from helping with a hacking campaign.
“They compromise a third party and they put models on that third party. They do that instead of using, say, a commercial option where their activities are observed,” Hultquist told NBC News.

The White House has repeatedly cast the U.S. and China as being in a race to develop the most cutting-edge AI. Both American and Chinese AI companies have announced this year that they have developed AI agents that are adept at hacking and cybersecurity operations.

In the last several months, both OpenAI and Anthropic have reported that their own AI agents have slipped out of evaluation sandboxes to reach third-party organizations — incidents that were disclosed after the fact. Google says it has not seen threat actors wage fully automated hacking campaigns but that instead, hacking groups are continuing to layer on more AI into their operations.

To date, there have been no publicly identified government hacking operations conducted entirely by AI agents. But China’s increasing reliance on agentic AI that it has installed on hacked computer networks means the country’s hackers — like any with sufficient resources and who aren’t legally constrained from such activity — can automate more of their work, Hultquist said.

“There were a couple cases where we could see them essentially trying to build out autonomous capabilities, so they can remove themselves, remove humans from the loop on some of their most important tasks,” Hultquist said.

title: Family of 14-year-old found dead in singer D4vd’s Tesla seeks the death penalty
summary: The family of Celeste Rivas Hernandez is calling for the singer D4vd to face the death penalty after a Los Angeles judge ordered him to stand trial in the killing of the 14-year-old.
story: The family of Celeste Rivas Hernandez is calling for the singer D4vd to face the death penalty after a Los Angeles judge ordered him to stand trial in the killing of the 14-year-old, whose dismembered remains were found in the trunk of his Tesla last year.

“If the death penalty were activated, it would be perfect for this kind of human being, devoid of feelings and emptiness inside, and without conscience, who only caused pain to our daughter, our family, and the world that supports our precious daughter,” the teen’s parents said in a statement Monday via their attorney.
They released the statement on what would have been her 16th birthday. An attorney for the singer, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In a separate statement, the family said they were “experiencing so many emotions” and “reliving unforgettable moments even though she is no longer here.”
“These are feelings that only a father and mother and her siblings can share, with a heavy heart. We will always remember every moment and every good time we spent with Celestita,” the family said.

The teen’s body was found in the front trunk of Burke’s Tesla at a Los Angeles impound lot in September 2025. Prosecutors said the car had been left on a street near Burke’s home and impounded at Hollywood Tow after someone reported an abandoned vehicle.
A decomposed head and torso were found in a black cadaver bag, according to court documents, and a second bag contained additional dismembered body parts.

Burke, 21, was arrested in April at a house on Marmont Avenue in the Hollywood Hills, Los Angeles police said. He has pleaded not guilty to charges of murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under the age of 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains.

At an evidentiary hearing in July, prosecutors said Burke began a relationship with Rivas Hernandez when she was 13 and ended it after she threatened to expose him. Text messages revealed in court showed that the teen had gotten pregnant by Burke and had an abortion.

Last month, Burke abruptly parted ways with his legal team and asked to be represented by public defenders. An attorney for Rivas Hernandez’s family said in a statement that he does not deserve a public defender given his status and fame on social media.

“The residents of Los Angeles County should be outraged because it will be the taxpayers that are picking up the tab to defend this millionaire,” attorney Patrick Steinfeld said. “David Anthony Burke is not indigent.”

title: New Mexico Democrats push back over Trump posts about renaming state ‘New America’
summary: New Mexico Democratic leaders are aggressively pushing back on President Donald Trump’s social media posts about renaming the state of New Mexico as “New America.”
story: New Mexico Democratic leaders are aggressively pushing back on President Donald Trump’s social media posts about renaming the state of New Mexico as “New America.”

“New Mexico’s name isn’t up for debate — it’s been ours since before the United States existed,” New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham, a Democrat, said in a post on X featuring an image of the state labeled with “New Mexico.” “While the President tries to distract Americans from his disastrous war in Iran, the price of gas —and everything else — keeps rising.

“Under Democratic leadership here in New Mexico, we’re providing families with free childcare and college, protecting access to health care and investing in housing,” the governor continued. “While the White House wastes time coloring on maps, Nuevo México is busy doing the work. 🌶️”

Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland, the Democratic nominee for governor who is vying to succeed Lujan Grisham in November, wrote on X, “I will always stand up for what makes New Mexico, New Mexico” with a video of her at a campaign event.

“The only thing I can think of think about when I see that is my opponent, because he’s a Republican, he’s running for New America,” Haaland says in the video. “I’m running to be the governor of New Mexico.”
Haaland’s GOP opponent, Gregg Hull, also rejected Trump’s suggestion.

“New Mexico does not need a new name,” Hull said in a statement, according to local news outlets. “This state carries the history of Native nations and Spanish explorers who named this land nearly five hundred years ago, and generations of families who built New Mexico into what is is today. That identity is not up for negotiation.”

Trump has prompted outrage among New Mexico Democrats and some Republicans when he posted a series of images on Truth Social depicting the state being renamed as “New America.” In an AI-generated post on Sunday, Trump is shown slapping a “New America” over a “Welcome to New Mexico” sign, as he does his signature Trump dance.

“Many people suggested changing the name of New Mexico, one of the great vote cheating states of all time, to NEW AMERICA,” Trump wrote in the post. “So much more prestigious and beautiful for the people of that potentially incredible State. Wow, I Love It!!!”
On Monday, he continued to post several more images on Truth Social, depicting New Mexico as New America.

His latest posts fit a pattern from his presidency, with Trump moving to rename other places on the map. A little more than a week ago, he signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” amid a U.S.-Canada trade war.

In January 2025, on his first day back in office, Trump signed an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.” He also renamed Denali, the highest peak in North America, as “Mount McKinley,” after the 25th president.
The move infuriated Alaska lawmakers, including those from Trump’s own party.

Of course, the president cannot unilaterally change the name of a state the way he can order the federal government to change how it refers to a mountain or a body of water in government databases and documents. The name is spelled out in the opening lines of the state’s constitution: “The name of this state is New Mexico …”
To change the name, New Mexico’s voters would need to amend the state constitution.
Both of New Mexico’s Democratic senators rejected Trump’s latest posts.
“Three things I will always call by their actual names … The Gulf of Mexico, Lake Ontario, New Mexico,” wrote Sen. Martin Heinrich.
“It’s New Mexico, always has been and always will be,” added Sen. Ben Ray Lujan. “Just like how you’ll always be a sinvergüenza and corrupt,” he added, using the Spanish word for scoundrel.
Rep. Melanie Stansbury, D-N.M., was perhaps the most blunt of the New Mexico lawmakers:
“Oh hell no!” she posted on X. “Our state’s name carries generations of history, culture, and family—and it belongs to us. We’re New Mexicans. Period.”

title: As Trump pushes for data centers, voters in key midterm races say they don’t want them
summary: An NBC News Decision Desk Poll found that 69% of respondents oppose building AI data centers in their areas, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea.
story: DES MOINES, Iowa — Dawn Vogel, a Republican county supervisor in rural Buchanan County, Iowa, doesn’t have a lot in common with the leading democratic socialists in Congress. But on this bit of policy they agree: Data centers are proliferating across the American landscape too fast.

Vogel voted earlier this year for a moratorium that temporarily bans data centers from setting up shop in her heavily Republican county, which favored President Donald Trump 63% to 35% in 2024. In Washington, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt. — the nation’s two most prominent democratic socialists — have proposed a similar moratorium that would cover the entire country.

“I don’t think this is a Republican or Democratic issue,” Vogel said on the sidelines of the Iowa State Association of Counties’ annual conference here in late August, adding that she hasn’t talked to a single voter at home who wants data centers.

“It’s an issue of what’s the best use for the land, what’s the best use for our natural resources,” she said. “You can have all the data you want to in the world, but if you don’t have water to drink, you don’t have humans to use the data.”

That point of view places Vogel in a loose, but very large, populist coalition that is fighting the rise of data centers at the ballot box, with yard signs, in courts and at all levels of government as November’s midterm elections approach.

An NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey, conducted from Aug. 20 through Sept. 1, found that 69% of respondents oppose the construction of AI data centers in their local area, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea.
They are all at odds with President Donald Trump.

“The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post at the end of August. “If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.”

But it’s more about backyards than being seen as backward, according to voters who spoke to NBC News on a recent road trip along Interstate 80 from Nebraska to New Jersey — a swath that includes eight swing districts key to determining which party will control the House next year and two marquee Senate races. These voters, who span the political spectrum, said they don’t want data centers anywhere near their communities.
More coverage of NBC News' 'Drive to Decision Day' road trip along I-80

Trump voters express rare frustration with the president: ‘He went against some of his promises’Republicans weigh whether to vote for Rep. Max Miller amid abuse allegations he deniesNew Jersey and PennsylvaniaOhioIowa and OhioIowa State FairNebraska

For some, the issue has become a touchstone for the feeling that the powerful are taking advantage of the powerless.

“All of the data centers that are starting to pop up in areas, I find that troublesome because it drives utility costs for citizens in the area,” said Tamara Clark, 49, a Democratic voter who works in the healthcare industry. “I don’t feel like the rich should continuously get rich while we have to grovel for what we need in our everyday necessities.”

In Clark’s congressional district, Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, a 22-term incumbent, is using the issue against her rival, Republican Derek Merrin, who cast a 2017 vote in the state Legislature that helped extend tax breaks to companies that build data centers in the state.

Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, who is seeking to hold his seat against Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown, was a full-throated advocate for data centers when he was the state’s lieutenant governor. But in July, he introduced legislation in the Senate that would require utility companies to charge large-scale data center operators enough money to cover the costs of increased electricity and water use.

His change of tune reflects a broader shift among elected officials who embraced data centers as a way to bring jobs and tax revenue to their cities, counties and states. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, D-Pa., who is on the ballot in November, signed a new batch of data center regulations in August after having encouraged companies to locate them in his state.

While Republican voters are more supportive of data centers than Democrats and independents, the majority of them remain opposed — 57% to 43% — according to the NBC News Decision Desk poll. The survey found that 81% of Democrats and 71% of independents are against data centers being built in their communities.
While supporters have been less demonstrative, their ranks extend beyond the AI companies building data centers and the politicians who have looked to them as economic development engines.

National and local labor unions involved in the construction and maintenance of data centers tout them as a boon for workers, both as a source of jobs and for high rates of pay. Several data center workers in Ohio spoke to NBC News about those benefits on the condition of anonymity because, according to one of them, they have agreed not to discuss their jobs with the media.
That worker said he can make as much as $5,000 in a week, including overtime, at a relatively low-level union job.

“It’s helping a lot of people — a lot of work going on, a lot of people benefiting from it,” the data center worker said, adding that he was warned by friends about problems, from overuse of water resources to weird ringing sounds, that he has not witnessed at his workplace.

“It’s scary,” he said. “You got a lot of people that say all these horrific things. I was told all these negative things about data centers, and then I started working at one, and I didn’t see any of the things I was told about.”

He said he would like to see proponents and critics work together to fix any problems with data centers so that they can continue to be built and operate without disruption to the surrounding communities.
But Jordan Cloe, 47, an electrician from Bondurant, in Iowa’s hotly contested 3rd Congressional District, said he’s worried about the resources used by a data center in neighboring Altoona.

“Did we have any data on what the implications were about water consumption or anything? Like, we just built a power grid where that thing sits,” he said. “Did we get to use that? No, they gobbled that up.”

Cloe, who said he aligns more with Democrats, said he doesn’t know anything about Sarah Trone Garriott, the Democratic challenger to Republican Rep. Zach Nunn, but that he plans to vote for her in November.
For Vogel, the county supervisor, the unresolved questions are enough reason to keep data centers out of her county — at least for now.
“We need to do what’s best for Buchanan County and then, you know, if the companies want to come knock on the door,” she said, “then we’ll talk.”

title: From ‘Traitors’ to Red Carpet Debut, Phaedra Parks and CT Tamburello’s Relationship Timeline
summary: Fans shipped Chris “CT” Tamburello of “Real World” fame and “Real Housewives” alum Phaedra Parks when they appeared on “The Traitors.” Now the pair admitted that they are dating.
story: Chris “CT” Tamburello of “Real World” fame may have won Season 2 of Peacock’s “The Traitors” competition show, but he also began a connection that blossomed long after leaving the Scottish castle: he is in a relationship with fellow contestant Phaedra Parks, a mortician and “Real Housewives” alum.
Yes, that’s right — the chemistry that fans of the show spotted on screen eventually led to a relationship off-screen.
Could “faithful” fans have possibly willed this relationship into existence? We’ll never know ... but we can hope!
So, how did these “traitors” become “faithful” to each other? Here’s a timeline of key moments in Parks and Tamburello’s relationship.
Fall 2023: Parks and Tamburello Meet While Filming ‘The Traitors’
Tamburello, 46, and Parks, 52, film Season 2 of “The Traitors” on location in Scotland.
The second season of the show featured familiar faces — and notable rivals — from popular reality TV programs.

Tamburello made his way to the cast via MTV. He first appeared on “The Real World: Paris” then went on to find success on “The Challenge.” Per People, he has won “The Challenge” five times (plus two spinoff seasons) and competed in 19 seasons.
His “Challenge” rival, Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio, also competed in this season of “The Traitors.”

The witty and outspoken Parks starred on “The Real Housewives of Atlanta” from 2010 to 2017, as well as in 2025 and 2026. She now dabbles in several projects, and on her Instagram page, she describes herself as an “attorney to the stars,” mommy, mortician, model, actress and author.
On both shows, she sparred for screen time with fellow Atlanta “Housewives” star Shereé Whitfield.
Early 2024: ‘The Traitors’ Premieres — and Fans Watch Their Connection Unfold
Episodes of Season 2 of “The Traitors” aired from January to March 2024.
The vibes between the two were noticeable.

Tamburello may have a tough Boston accent, but he seemed to turn into a softie around Parks. And while Parks could eviscerate an opponent in 30 seconds or less, she seemed surprisingly sweet on Tamburello, calling him her “Castle Daddy.”

Tamburello ultimately helped remove Parks from the castle, but as he voted for her as a Traitor, he smiled and said, “I think you came on here to be the opposite of who you are in real life. And I think you’ve been the best Traitor we’ve seen yet.”
March 2024: These Fan Favorites Comment on Their Chemistry During Press Tour
In an interview that spring, Vulture flat out told Parks, “So the internet wants you and CT to be boyfriend and girlfriend.”
Parks replied, “Oh, god.”

She went on to say, “CT is a great guy, and we definitely had a wonderful connection. He’s a sweetheart. He’s a really good guy, and he’s attractive and all those good things. He’s a gentleman. There was never anything romantic between us at all. It was just a sweet, pure friendship.”
Tamburello shared similar sentiments in an interview with Entertainment Weekly in March 2024.

“No, nothing real happened, I’ll be honest with you,” he said in the interview. “It was fun. I loved her because she’s a cornball. She was great. I would say there was a sense of sincerity, for sure. But it was also playing a game, you know?”
August 2026: Parks Admits She Might Have More Than a Friendship With Tamburello
During a Sept. 4 appearance on “Jeff Lewis Live,” Parks said that she would be attending the Emmys with a date that was “not” platonic.
Admittedly wanting to make a splash with their relationship, Parks withholds details but shared that something has been brewing with a mysterious “CT” for a while.
A caller piped up to “connect the dots” for everyone.

“They were on ‘The Traitors’ together. She called him her ‘castle daddy’ on the show,” said a caller identified only as Megan. “So I know you want to wait to disclose it to the world, but please don’t plead the fifth. Let us know if it’s that CT.”
“Ummmm ... I think so,” Parks replied hesitantly.
Lewis confirmed that he could see Tamburello outside the studio, and that the “CT” Parks mentioned was definitely her “Traitors” competitor.
September 2026: Tamburello and Parks Hard Launch Relationship on the Red Carpet
Phaedra Parks doesn’t do anything halfway, and the hard launch of her relationship with Tamburello is no exception.
The pair stunned on the red carpet at the first night of the 78th Emmy Awards in Los Angeles on Sept. 5.

Along with photos from the evening, Parks posted this comment on her Instagram page on Sept. 6: “Some came for the awards. I came with the prize. Thank you to the real trophy for making a beautiful night even better.”
Fellow “Traitors” contestant and occasional “Challenge” rival Devenanzio used the same comment and hilariously paired it on Instagram with photos of him and Tamburello from the same event.
Parks posted a response: “We are a thropple.”

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Teases James and Oliver Phelps As New Castle Keepers
summary: A first look at James and Oliver Phelps, known as Fred and George Weasley in “Harry Potter” films, as Alan Cumming’s castle keepers in “The Traitors: New Blood.”
story: “The Traitors” is gearing up for its first season filled with “every day Americans” — and it appears host Alan Cumming is getting help from some famous twins.
TODAY has an exclusive first look at the new castle keepers in “The Traitors: New Blood,” James and Oliver Phelps.

Best known for playing Fred and George Weasley in the “Harry Potter” films, the actors will keep an eye on Cumming’s castle as he welcomes the new recruits and puts them through the ultimate game of deceit.
The clip, shared Sept. 7, begins with a glimpse at the reality show’s famous Scottish castle before a phone rings and one of the Phelps brothers answers.
“Keeper, is the castle set?” Cumming is heard asking, with one brother replying, “It is, Alan” while the other also makes an appearance and adds, “Oh, it is Alan.”
The brothers then raise the castle flag as Cumming says, “Let the games begin.”

While the U.S. version of “The Traitors” has only featured celebrities over its four seasons, “New Blood” will welcome 22 civilians into the Scottish Highlands castle. The cast along with their mischievous portraits were revealed on Aug. 12.

Once there, the game is the same with the contestants either chosen as a Traitor or Faithful. Determined to win the $250,000 prize, the Faithfuls will then seek out the Traitors and attempt to not get eliminated (aka “murdered”), while the Traitors try to deceit the Faithfuls and not get banished from the castle. As for James and Oliver Phelps, the actors will be on hand to help the competition be as treacherous as ever.
“The Traitors: New Blood” premieres Sept. 17 on NBC at 8 p.m. with back-to-back episodes. They will be available to stream the next day on Peacock.
New episodes will air every Thursday at the same time on the network.
(Peacock and NBC are owned by NBCUniversal, TODAY’s parent company).

title: Oasis Frontmen and Brothers Liam Gallagher and Noel Gallagher Reunite on Red Carpet Following Feud
summary: The Gallagher brothers, Liam and Noel, made a rare appearance on the red carpet on Sept. 5 at the Venice International Film Festival screening of “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.”
story: British band members and brothers Noel Gallagher, 59, and Liam Gallagher, 53, are responsible for megahits like “Wonderwall,” “Champagne Supernova” and the titular “Don’t Look Back in Anger.” Despite their success, the band split more than a decade ago due to the all-too-frequent feuds.

The Gallagher brothers made a rare appearance on the red carpet on Sept. 5 at the Venice International Film Festival screening of “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger,” a new documentary about the behind-the-scenes drama surrounding their highly anticipated 41-date reunion tour in 2025.
The documentary opens in theaters on Sept. 11.
Could the tour have brought the brothers closer together? Perhaps. They certainly seemed at ease on the Venice red carpet, smiling, hugging, pulling faces and even holding hands in a victory pose.
Noel Gallagher even got playful and stuck his tongue out at the photographers during the red carpet.
Oasis had been broken up since August 2009 following a reported brawl between the two. Noel Gallagher then announced he was quitting the band after a show at a festival in Paris.
While the two had pursued their own solo careers, they announced their reunion tour in August 2024.
This is not the first time post-breakup that the brothers seem to have found a new rhythm together.
Last August, Noel Gallagher told the British radio show talkSPORT that his brother Liam Gallagher has been “amazing” and “smashing it.”
That was quite a turnaround for the brothers, who frequently sparred on social media and in interviews over the years.
“I guess when it’s all said and done, we’ll sit and reflect on it, but it’s great being back in a band with Liam,” Noel Gallagher said in the interview. “I forgot how funny he was.”
He continued, “Liam’s smashing it, and I’m proud of him.”

Noel Gallagher, who had been working as a solo artist alongside his band the High Flying Birds following Oasis’ breakup, added about his brother, “I’ve got to say, I kind of look at him and think, ‘Good for you, mate.’ He’s been amazing.”

title: Behind Raygun’s ‘Cringe’ Olympic Breakdancing Routine Is An Oddly Sweet Love Story
summary: Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn — who’s better known under her stage name Raygun — competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, becoming the center of ridicule. But husband Samuel Free stuck by her side.
story: When Australian breakdancer Rachael Gunn — who’s better known under her stage name Raygun — competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics, she became the focus of memes, ridicule and a deluge of parodies.
But one person wasn’t laughing. In fact, unlike pretty much all of social media at the time, he found her moves rather breathtaking.

Samuel Free, Gunn’s husband and coach, is among the key figures featured in the new Netflix documentary “Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly,” which chronicles the events around the viral routine that set social media aflame.

The documentary, which was released Sept. 1, includes voices from other dancers who were less-than-impressed by Gunn’s breakdancing skills. But Free stands fiercely by Gunn’s moves, which included some, uh, odd choices like the sprinkler and a pose meant to mimic a kangaroo. He goes so far as to say that he was captivated by her routine.
“I was struck by the beauty of her performance,” Free says in the documentary of her Olympics appearance.
Free’s comments in the documentary have prompted social media users to describe the two as a match made in heaven, with some even hoping to find the same level of devotion in a partner.
“May all of us have partners as supportive as Raygun‘s husband was at the Olympics,” one social media user wrote on Threads.

Raygun went viral after her two performances in Paris did not earn a single point from the judges across four rounds. There, she lost by a combined 36-0 to two competitors. And her moves elicited everything from memes to Halloween costumes.
How Did Raygun Meet Her Husband, Samuel Free?
Raygun’s connection to the sport actually goes back to Free, who is responsible for introducing her to breakdancing, the documentary shows.
Free, a breakdancer himself, once competed under the name Sammy Sex. He says in the doc that he became drawn to the art form at an early age when he watched the 1984 film “Breakin.’”
“They’re doing big moves,” Free says. “I didn’t even know people could do this!”

He says he kept up with breakdancing through the years, which ended up being a “sticking point” in many of his romantic relationships throughout his 20s — that is, until he met Gunn while working at a call center.
“I have a life-changing moment,” Free recalls of meeting Gunn. “I remember walking past this girl in the break room.”

The two ended up hitting it off, according to the film. Gunn, who was in college at the time, says that Free “opened up my world.” For Gunn, one particularly pivotal moment was when he took her to a breaking battle, she says.
“Walking into this space felt like I walked into a movie,” Gunn says in the documentary.
It was after that battle, during which she was inspired by one of the women dancers, that she decided that she wanted to pursue breakdancing. And right by her side was Free.

“Sammy was my cheer squad, my fan, my biggest supporter,” Gunn, a university lecturer whose research revolved around breaking as well, says in the film. “He’s special ... makes you feel like you can do things when you’re around him.”
Free, who eventually started to coach her, says that they began “building a life together.” And in 2018, the two got married.
“Our wedding was so beautiful,” Gunn says over footage from their big day, which appeared to include quite a bit of craziness on the dance floor. “We were just so happy.”
How Did Free Help His Wife Prepare For The Olympics?
The two speak in the film about their experience preparing for the Olympics after Gunn had qualified to represent Oceania. They say that Gunn hit the gym and Free pushed her to train hard.
“I was like, ‘As your husband, I am in awe of how hard you’re working. Props to you. As your coach, you need to work harder. This is not clean,’” Free recounts.

In the lead-up to Paris, the couple says that they realized it was unlikely she’d best any of the other competitors. So instead of focusing on power moves — like windmills and headspins, for example — they decided to take a different approach. Free suggested they shift the routine into an ode to Australia, helping her incorporate moves reminiscent of swimming and the now-infamous kangaroo freeze, they recount.
While in Paris, some others were weary of what Gunn had planned to do, Free was stoked.
“This is Rachael’s moment. It’s her saying, ‘I’m doing me,’” Free says.
What Did Raygun’s Husband Think Of The Aftermath Of The Performance?

The aftermath of Gunn’s performance was pretty ugly, the documentary shows. And Free says that the onslaught of memes, trolling and bullying from the internet was a “massive trauma.” At the time conspiracies spread that Free was on the committee that had chosen Gunn to represent their country in the Olympics — something that’s been shot down by organizers, other competitors and the couple themselves. Still, the two spent a few months in the Netherlands in an attempt to lie low and recover from the incident.
It’s been a while since the 2024 Paris games, and Gunn admits that she was “cringe.”
“I brought shame and embarrassment on the country,” she says.
However, she underscores that she’s still dancing and that “Paris hasn’t defeated me.” As for Free, he’s still standing right by her side.
He says that his wife’s “performance connected with people, whether that’s genuine excitement and entertainment or outrage.”
“It generated discourse and got the entire world talking,” he says.

title: After ‘Ted Lasso’ Feature, Negro Leagues Baseball Museum ‘Can Hardly Handle’ Surge In Visitors, Its President Says
summary: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, which preserves the long history of African American baseball in the U.S., was featured in the premiere of the new season of “Ted Lasso” in August. And it’s been flooded with visitors ever since.
story: Kansas City, Missouri’s Negro Leagues Baseball Museum is now dealing with a good problem to have.

The historical institution, which preserves the long history of African American baseball in the U.S., was featured in the premiere of the new season of “Ted Lasso” in August. And since, the museum’s president Bob Kendrick tells TODAY.com, the establishment has been flooded with visitors. Sales, Kendrick says, are up around 50% to 60% compared to where they were last year at this time.

“I’ll tell you — it has superseded anything that I could have ever even remotely imagined,” Kendrick says of the outpouring of interest in the museum from the show. “I honestly did not know that it would have this kind of interest and immediate impact on the museum.”

While the show’s third season, which wrapped in May 2023, ended with star and co-creator Jason Sudeikis’ character Ted Lasso leaving his life in the UK for Kansas City, the new season is all about his hop back across the pond. This time, Ted is tasked with helping to lead AFC Richmond women’s soccer team, the Lady Greyhounds, to success.

But the first episode of the new season doesn’t start in the UK. Ted, who’s now working in a grocery store and parenting his son, still needs some convincing to leave the stability behind for the coaching gig abroad. And several of his old friends, including Rebecca, Keeley and Higgins, show up in KC to do just that.

While there, Higgins, played by Jeremy Swift, attempts to hit up the American Jazz Museum — which is housed in the same building as the NLBM — but finds it unexpectedly closed for the day. So he ends up taking a tour of the baseball establishment and becomes wildly moved by the figures he’s introduced to. One of these impactful players is the legendary Satchel Paige, widely recognized as one of the best pitchers in the history of the game. Paige’s career in the Negro Leagues began the 1920s.

“Satchel was a showman. He had a wild throwing style and all these crazy names for his pitches. ‘The Hesitation.’ The Midnight Creeper.’ ‘The Dipsy-Do’,” an NLBM employee, played by actor Milan Carter, tells Higgins. “Many thought old Satch would be the first to break the major league color barrier. He wasn’t. But he finally got in at the age of 42. Oldest rookie in history, and he was still incredible.”
As the NLBM staff member says in the show, “the Negro Leagues were glorious.”

“They didn’t do it for fame or fortune. They did it ‘cause to not play would have been unacceptable,” the staff member says of the leagues, which were formed in 1920 as a response to a decades-long unwritten “gentleman’s agreement” between club owners that kept Black players out of all professional leagues with white players.

The visit leaves a huge impression on Higgins, who is seen later in the episode, decked out in a Kansas City Monarchs jersey. The Monarchs were one of the most successful teams in the Negro Leagues and boasted Paige as one of its alumni.
Kendrick tells TODAY.com that the episode’s representation of the museum was moving.

“The scene was so beautifully done,” Kendrick says. “The care, the concern, the understanding of the essence of what Negro Leagues history represented both on and off the field —you saw that in that scene.”
The only complaint he’s gotten?

“I got a lot of calls, people ask me why wasn’t I in it. Because they wanted me to be the guy that was talking about Satchel Paige,” he says, before laughing. “What I told him was, ‘Number one, you never play yourself. You go find somebody who’s younger and better looking for you.’”
Kendrick explains that the NLBM scenes were filmed about a year ago. Back then, he says he had no idea what would happen after the episode aired.

“Perhaps I was a little bit naive on just how big this show really is,” he says. “It has just absolutely captivated the hearts and the imaginations of ‘Lasso’ fans around the world, and it obviously has exposed Negro League’s history and this museum to millions of people around the globe.”
Kendrick, who met Sudeikis years ago at a holiday ceremony, says that the “Ted Lasso” creator has visited the museum and been a fan for some time.

“There are many great attractions here in Kansas City, and for Jason to write us into this this love letter to Kansas City speaks volumes about what this museum meant to him,” he says. “I was here on the set when they were shooting it, so I had seen it already. I saw it in real time, but when I saw it in the show, it was very emotional for me.”

Now that Paige has even more fans, Kendrick says that there’s a plethora of Negro Leagues stars that people can look into, like the great Martín Dihigo, perhaps the most versatile player in baseball history. Dihigo, whose nickname is “El Maestro,” hailed from Cuba and began playing professionally in 1922.

“He was essentially Shohei Ohtani before we ever knew who Shohei Ohtani was. Martín Dihigo played all nine positions and played all nine of them well,” Kendrick says, referencing the current Los Angeles Dodgers two-way phenom.

He added that Dihigo is among the only baseball players “in the history of our sport to be enshrined into five different countries’ baseball halls of fame. He’s in the Mexican, Cuban, Venezuelan, Dominican, and in Cooperstown.”

As more people continue to be introduced to the museum through “Ted Lasso,” Kendrick says that the institution’s existing plans to expand and move out of their current space has become even more important.

“A new, much larger, expansive Negro Leagues baseball museum is looming on the horizon,” he says. “I need more space now to handle all these people and to expand on the stories that we have and to tell new stories.”

title: Patriots Cheerleaders Join Savannah Bananas’ ‘Dad Bod Cheer Squad’ For Epic Routine
summary: During a recent Savannah Bananas baseball game, the team’s official “Dad Bod Cheer Squad” known as the Man-Nanas, joined forces with the New England Patriots cheerleaders at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts for a routine that’s been scoring big with fans.
story: It’s the collab we never knew we needed.

During a recent Savannah Bananas baseball game, the team’s official “Dad Bod Cheer Squad” known as the Man-Nanas, joined forces with the New England Patriots cheerleaders at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts for a routine that’s been scoring big with fans.
The grand slam of a number has gone viral with nearly four million views on Instagram alone as of Sept. 6, since it was posted just over a day prior. And after seeing it, you’ll understand why.
The video begins with the Patriots cheerleaders, performing to a mashup of several songs including Destiny’s Child’s “Lose My Breath, Missy Elliott’s “Lose Control” and Beyoncé’s “Formation.”
Pretty soon, the Man-Nanas join the fun. And together, the parties crush the routine as the stadium explodes into cheers.
It’s pretty difficult to decide who does it better. As the caption says, it’s “safe to say @the_man_nanas gave the @patriotscheerleaders a run for their money 😉”
The performance was part of the Savannah Bananas’ two-night series against the Loco Beach Coconuts at Gillette Stadium on Aug. 28 and 29.

The team, which has amassed a following for their viral dance numbers and unique spin on the sport, which they call “Banana Ball,”  also invited several others for memorable performances during the series including country star Keith Urban. According to the team’s social media accounts, the event was popular, selling out both nights with 130,000 fans.

title: Bindi Irwin Posts Sweet Video of Dad Steve Irwin Reflecting on Her Birth, 20 Years After His Death
summary: Bindi Irwin, daughter of Australian wildlife conservationist and television personality Steve Irwin, honored her father on the recent 20th anniversary of his death.
story: Bindi Irwin, daughter of Australian wildlife conservationist and television personality Steve Irwin, honored her father on the recent 20th anniversary of his death.
Bindi Irwin shared an emotional Instagram post Sept. 4 in remembrance of her father, who died in 2006 after a stingray pierced his heart with a poisonous barb.

The post not only included some moving words about the beloved Steve Irwin’s impact on her life and the greater movement around conservation but also a heartbreakingly beautiful video of the “Crocodile Hunter,” reflecting on her birth — something he called “the most incredible wildlife encounter of my life.”
Bindi Irwin, who’s now a zookeeper and conservationist herself, wrote in the caption that “20 years ago, today, the world lost the most passionate and dedicated wildlife conservationist.”

“Our family lost our superhero. My mum lost the love of her life; my brother and I lost the greatest dad. Grief never truly leaves us; we walk alongside it every day,” Bindi Irwin wrote of her father, who died at age 44. “Where there is enormous grief, there is even greater love. In the last 20 years, I have watched the world mourn my dad with our family.
She added that she had “always thought that my dad’s legacy is wildlife conservation.”
“It turns out, his legacy is love,” Bindi Irwin wrote. “For our planet and for each other.”

In the video, Steve Irwin takes viewers through the story of Bindi Irwin’s birth in July 1998. He explains that the obstetrician, “an absolute legend of a man,” encouraged him to help with the delivery. After a bit of teamwork, Steve Irwin recalls, his daughter was born.
“I swear she’s fitted right in here in the palms of my hands,” Steve Irwin says in the video. “I was flabbergasted.”

He also explains that his daughter’s name comes from that of his favorite crocodile Bindi. His wife Terri Irwin added the middle name Sue after the couple’s dog Sui, who often made appearances on television alongside Steve Irwin.

“So Bindi Sue Irwin.  ... It was a combination of adrenaline and just emotion,” he says in the video. “It was like a euphoric feeling. I was in total utopia. We both were. To bring this little person into the world. For me to deliver my daughter was a very special moment. I can’t dwell on it too long because I start to cry. It was so special.”
Steve Irwin adds that after he cut the umbilical cord, he couldn’t help but pick up his baby girl and show her off to everyone in the hospital.

“I’ve grabbed that little thing, that little baby, and we’re in the maternity ward of a very special hospital where a lot of women have given birth,” he recalls. “And I ran around the hospital, ‘Look at this! Look at this!’”
The nurses and other mothers in the ward were already well acquainted with the concept of a newborn, he adds.
“And they’re like, “Yes, we’ve got our own,’” he remembers them saying. “’Yeah, but you haven’t got one like this one! Look at this little beauty! Look at this little beauty!”
He says he is “the proudest father on the face of the earth, no doubt.”

Steve Irwin passed away when Bindi Irwin was 8 years old. Her brother, Robert Irwin, was almost three years old. His death occurred during the filming of documentary “Ocean’s Deadliest,” which was released in 2007.
Bindi Irwin wrote in her post that her 5-year-old daughter, Grace Warrior Irwin Powell, watches Steve Irwin’s documentaries every morning.

“She feels utterly loved by her ‘grandpa crocodile’ without ever having met him. My dad left a lasting impact so poignant that it will ripple out for generations to come,” she wrote. “I believe with my whole heart that his love will live on forever. In all of us. In every kindness we show to the Earth. And that is a life and legacy worth celebrating.”
Bindi Irwin concluded the emotional post with a message to her late father.

“Dad, I love you with my whole heart. Thank you for being our guardian angel,” Bindi Irwin wrote. “And most of all, thank you for watching over my daughter now, too. She loves you so much. We all do.”

Other members of the Irwin family have paid tribute to Steve Irwin, including his wife Terri Irwin. The couple, who met in 1991, married the following year, according to the family’s website. In lieu of a honeymoon, they embarked on a crocodile rescue mission.
Terri Irwin wrote in an Instagram post Sept. 4 that “grief still walks with me like my shadow.”

“With the passing of time I have gained more perspective and understanding. We were together as a family, on our crocodile research expedition, for what was to be our final six weeks together,” Terri Irwin wrote. “Ours was to be a long and sweet goodbye. Steve spent time with Bindi and Robert building swings and climbing trees. We all slowed down. Time slowed down.”
She concluded her post, calling on fans to treasure their loved ones.
“I believe that all of us, every one of us, gets to say goodbye,” Terri Irwin wrote. “We just may not know that we’re saying it. Hold every moment dear with the ones you love. Until we meet again.❤️”

title: How Megan Moroney’s First Heartbreak Kickstarted Her Music Career
summary: Megan Moroney’s rise in the country music scene was fueled by teenage heartbreak and a trip to Guitar Center, she tells Willie Geist.
story: Megan Moroney’s rise in the country music scene was fueled by teenage heartbreak and a trip to Guitar Center.

The 28-year-old, behind hits like “Bless Your Heart” and “I’m Not Pretty,” has built a brand on vulnerable lyrics and all-things pink, leading to her current world tour. In between one of her “Cloud 9 Tour” stops in New York City, Moroney spoke to Willie Geist about the start of her success on TODAY’s Sunday Sitdown.
During their chat, the singer revealed that she inherited her music genes from her dad, who taught her to play guitar and also worked a second job as a musician.
Moroney, who grew up in Douglasville, Georgia, spoke to Willie about the pivotal moment in her childhood that prompted her to pick up a guitar.
“When I was, like, 16, I injured my knee in cheerleading. That’s why I have this gnarly scar right here,” she said, showing Willie the proof.
She continued, “I had nothing else to do but sit down and learn how to play guitar.”

She started learning how to play Deana Carter’s “Strawberry Wine.” But while she was trying to get a grasp of the instrument, she dealt with a second dose of bad luck — she experienced her first heartbreak.

“I got my first guitar, shortly after that, (I) got my heart broken for the first time. I wouldn’t stop crying, so my dad took me to Guitar Center,” she recalled. “And I remember there was a Memorial Day sale. But when I took the Taylor (guitar) down, my dad goes to pay for it. And (they’re) like, ‘Oh. This one’s not on sale.’”
Moroney was determined to get her hands on the instrument, so she had to work some magic.

“I remember looking at my dad. And I was like, ‘I’ve had my heart broken, once this week. I can handle it again, if you don’t want to get it for me.’ And that’s how I ended up with my first Taylor,” she shared and laughed.

That moment was the start of what has become a major country music career. Through her songs, Moroney’s fans are able to connect with her and relate to the relationship experiences she often reflects in her music.
Willie mentioned that Moroney refers to these intimate moments with her fans when she is on stage as “group therapy.”
Moroney said she uses that term because her shows feel as though she and her fans are together in a “collective effort,” to release their emotions.
“It’s very empowering to be in a room where everyone feels the same way, you know?” she pointed out. “It’s like, ‘Wow. This person got treated like s—, too.’ And we’re angry about it, together.”
Moroney also spoke about being an “overthinker,” a quality that she says has helped her develop her songwriting skills.
“That’s the best way that I’ve found to move on from things is when I take those emotions and I turn it into art. Now we all get to enjoy it,” she shared.
However, making music that reflects aspects of her personal life also brings interest and questions about her romances, especially around the subjects of her songs about love gone wrong, she said.
Moroney said she has become better at managing that side of stardom. But she added that she used to struggle with it.

“At that point, there were definitely nights where I would cry myself to sleep ‘cause I felt so misunderstood and I wanted to tell people everything,” she revealed when speaking about the early parts of her career.
It was challenging “trying to find the balance of not telling everyone my entire personal life, but also letting people know, like, ‘This is how I feel,’” Moroney said, laughing.
She mentioned her song “Who Hurt You?” from her third album “Cloud 9” as an example of a more private track.
“I purposely wrote it so that people wouldn’t ask me questions about it. If you listen to the song, (and) you still have questions, I got no answers for you,” she said.
Setting boundaries have come with age and a few years in the music industry, she said.
These days, she told Willie she has a newfound sense of confidence that is expressed in her newest album.

“I think it has a lot to do with me just getting a little bit older. I’m 28 now. So I trust myself a lot more. I think everyone can relate to when you grow up, you have a lot more experience and you trust that no matter what life throws at you, you’re gonna be OK,” she explained. “And being able to feel that way just kind of spilled into my writing, naturally, That’s where I’m at (in) life.”

title: Ariana Grande and Ricky Alvarez Are Back: Here’s Their Relationship Timeline
summary: Some Ariana Grande fans know Ricky Alvarez from when Grande was spotted alongside him licking a doughnut on a counter — a moment many online have referred to as “donutgate.”
story: Some Ariana Grande fans know Ricky Alvarez from when Grande was spotted alongside him licking a doughnut on a counter — a moment many online have referred to as “donutgate.” Other fans may know his name from his famous shoutout in her hit “Thank U, Next”: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh.”
Some may even recognize him from old concert videos, when he was a backup dancer on her first arena tour, “The Honeymoon Tour” in 2015, when their offstage public romance began.
Now, years later, Alvarez is once again the center of fandom conversations as Grande is seemingly back in a relationship with him, per recent buzzy Instagram posts and public sightings.
From backup dancer to boyfriend, breakup to rekindling, here’s a timeline of key moments in the relationship between Grande and Alvarez.
April 2014: Ricky Alvarez Becomes One of Ariana Grande’s Backup Dancers
Alvarez made his onstage debut with Grande while the pop star was in the middle of her own big moment: performing her hit song “Problem” for the first time live at the Radio Disney Music Awards.
At the time, Grande was rumored to be single, although she was spotted kissing former on-again-off-again beau Jai Brooks at the iHeart Radio Music Awards a month later.
February 2015: Ariana Grande Starts Her “Honeymoon Tour,” With Ricky Alvarez Backup Dancing
Grande kicked off her first arena tour with Alvarez as one of her male backup dancers.
June 2015: Relationship Rumors First Spark

Fans first started to speculate about a relationship between Grande and Alvarez after they shared an onstage kiss during New York City Pride, around a couple months after the singer reportedly split from rapper Big Sean.

In the months following the kiss, Grande proceeded to share romantic clips of the pair — including many of them goofing off together before and after shows, primarily on her now-defunct Snapchat account.
July 2015: The Famous “Donutgate” Unfolds
Alvarez was alongside the singer when she was captured on camera at Wolfee Donuts in California, licking a doughnut on the store’s counter and declaring “I hate America.”
In the same video, Grande is also captured kissing Alvarez — marking the couple’s first on-camera kiss following New York City Pride.
In an extended statement posted on X, Grande apologized to her fans and insisted, “I am EXTREMELY proud to be an American.”
She also said her comments were meant to be private, aimed at her friend who was purchasing the doughnuts, TODAY.com previously reported.
May 2016: Ariana Grande Releases “Dangerous Woman” Album, With Nods to Ricky Alvarez

When Grande released her third studio album “Dangerous Woman,” many fans speculated that some of the romance songs like “Moonlight,” “Knew Better/Forever Boy” and “Into You” were written about her then-beau.
In an interview with Billboard that same month, her longtime friend and co-writer Victoria Monet confirmed that “Moonlight” was based off a nickname Alvarez had given her.

“That’s what Ricky called her one night. I think it was after their first kiss,” Monet told the magazine. “He waited to kiss her for a long time, and she was really impressed. He’s such a gentleman, and the song is a great little bookmark of the start of their relationship.”
Grande’s comment to the publication was less detailed: “We’re happy. I’m a very happy girl. I have a healthy life right now, and I think that’s all anyone cares to know. The end.”
July 2016: Fans Speculate the Couple Split, Ariana Grande Posts Hinting Tweets
Grande first started to fuel breakup rumors when she took to then-Twitter to write “life is wild” and “change is f****** fantastic,” according to a fan account on Instagram.
The singer did not publicly confirm the breakup at the time.
November 2018: Ariana Grande Releases “Thank U, Next” With a Lyric for Ricky Alvarez, And He Reacts
Grande released her hit “Thank U, Next,” in which she name-dropped Alvarez alongside Big Sean, Pete Davidson and Mac Miller, her other former beaus.
“Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh,” she sang.
After the song came out, Alvarez posted an Instagram story reacting to his shoutout. In the clip, he zooms in on his face as Grande sings his name.
In a story posted right after, he wrote in part: “Nothing but gratitude ... those songs are fire tho... you’re welcome.”
January 2019: Ricky Alvarez Attended Ariana Grande’s “7 Rings” Release Party
Alvarez attended Grande’s party for the release of her hit single “7 Rings” and shared an Instagram photo from the festivities, posing with two photographers and directors from her team.
Grande commented “the best team see y’all on touuuur,” with two camera emojis.
February 2019: Ariana Grande Comments on Ricky Alvarez’ Reaction to “Thank U, Next” Feature
During her interview on the Zach Sang show, Grande responded to Alvarez’s initial reaction to her “Thank U, Next” lyric about him.

“Ricky loved it. He was proud. But Ricky was like, ‘Why did I get the worst line?’ And I was like, ‘What do you mean?’ He was like, ‘Everyone else’s line is so nice, and mine is like, ‘Man, f*** him, he’s trash,’” the singer recalled.
She continued: “I was like, ‘I could have said that, I could’ve said ‘Wrote some songs about Ricky,’ never mind he’s trash,’ But I didn’t. I said, ‘Now I listen and laugh.’”
March 2019: Ariana Grande Starts Her “Sweetener World Tour,” Ricky Alvarez Joins As A Photographer
Alvarez got back into professional work with Grande when she kicked off her “Sweetener World Tour.” He joined the crew as a photographer, per multiple fan reports.
April 2019: Ricky Alvarez Co-Directs Ariana Grande’s “Monopoly” Music Video, Photographs Her Coachella Performance

Alvarez took his camera work with Grande a step further when he collaborated with her longtime photographer and videographer Alfredo Flores to make a music video for “Monopoly,” her single with Victoria Monet.
After the video premiered, he took to Instagram to declare the song one of his “favorite slaps yet,” per his post’s caption.
Later that month, Alvarez photographed Grande’s headlining performances at Coachella.
He posted a photo he captured on Instagram from the first weekend, and the singer commented a praying emoji with a black heart.
June 2026: Ariana Grande Starts Changing “Thank U, Next” Lyrics About Ricky On Stage

Around seven years, several public relationships and one brief marriage later, Grande alluded to the pair’s potential rekindling — or at least friendship — when she first changed the lyric about him in “Thank U, Next” during her “Eternal Sunshine Tour” stop in Austin, Texas.
“Wrote some songs about Ricky / And they still kinda slap,” she sang.
Two nights later, she changed the lyrics again during her birthday show in the same city: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / I know he’s still got my back.”
Meanwhile, relationship rumors about the pair swirled as TMZ photographed the pair together multiple times throughout the summer.
At Grande’s Brooklyn, New York tour stop, she changed the lyrics again: “Wrote some songs about Ricky / We always find our way back.”
July 2026: Ricky Alvarez Includes Ariana Grande in an Instagram Post
